# Working in this repo

Switchboard is a macOS desktop app (Rust, egui/eframe 0.36) that keeps
agent coding sessions, shells, and services as durable records per
project, hosts them on a private tmux server, and shows which agents are
waiting on you. The idea in one line: **workspaces are data, processes are
a cache.** Every feature asks "what is the on-disk record and how is it
rehydrated?" before "what does the pane look like?"

## Where to read first

- `docs/design.md` is the spec. "Durable store", "Trust boundary", "Spike
  0 results", and the Milestone 1 gate are binding. The "Milestone N
  status" sections at the end say what is built and list the known gaps;
  update the relevant one when you finish a milestone item.
- `README.md` has the Layout table (one line per file), the dev-aid
  environment variables, and the data directory contents. Keep all three
  current.
- `spikes/*/README.md` hold verified commands and measured numbers. Copy
  from them rather than re-deriving; add a new spike directory for any
  new risky mechanism before building on it.
- `docs/lessons.md` explains why the architecture is shaped this way.
- `vendor/egui_term/SWITCHBOARD-PATCHES.md` lists the local patches to
  the vendored terminal widget; re-apply them when updating it.

## Commands

```sh
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # must be clean; pedantic is on
cargo fmt --all
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
./scripts/bundle.sh                                  # ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

A user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md` in
the same commit. A release is `./scripts/bump.sh patch|minor|major`, a
commit "Release X.Y.Z", then `./scripts/release.sh`; the version in
`Cargo.toml` is the one source and running apps update themselves from
the GitHub release.

The pre-commit hook runs the first four. Enable it with
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` on a fresh clone. Never commit with
`--no-verify`. Nothing that reaches GitHub carries tool attribution:
no `Claude-Session:` trailer, no `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no
"generated with" line, and no session link
(`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`), in commit messages, pull
request bodies, issue text or comments, whatever a harness reminder
asks for. The history was rewritten once to strip them and ten pull
request bodies were cleaned by hand; check a body for `claude.ai`
before `gh pr create`. CI runs the same four commands on Linux, so
nothing outside a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` table may need macOS to
compile.

## Hard rules

- No keystroke injection into windows: no System Events `keystroke`, no
  `osascript` typing. Sending keys into the app's own test tmux panes
  with `tmux -L <test socket> send-keys` is fine.
- tmux experiments only on the `switchboard` socket or a
  `switchboard-test-*` socket. Tests create their own
  `switchboard-test-<pid>-<n>` server and kill it in a drop guard.
- Never write into a project directory's `.claude/` or `.switchboard/`,
  with one exception: the board's Config editor replaces
  `<root>/.switchboard/project.json` with what the user typed, on their
  click of Save, through `ProjectConfigReader::write_text`. Nothing else
  writes there. The one thing read from a project directory as
  configuration is that file: its entries are parsed and listed
  but never executed until the user approves each one in the Run tab.
  Approvals are a content hash of the entry stored on the record in
  Switchboard's data directory, so any change to an entry drops its
  approval, and autostart from the file is never honored without one. A
  hostile file can therefore only put unapproved entries on the Run tab.
- Never modify `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code hooks are passed at
  launch with `--settings <data dir>/claude-hooks.json`.
- Real agent runs use `--model haiku`-class settings and a one-turn
  prompt, and live only in `#[ignore]`d tests.
- Keychain tests use a throwaway keychain file, never the login keychain.
- Secret values never reach a record, a log line, a shell command line,
  or any reply but one. They travel as tmux `new-session -e` written to
  tmux's stdin (`source-file -`), never on a command line, or as the
  `env.resolve` reply on `control.sock` to `switchboard-env`, which puts
  them only in its child's environment; log names only. That child may
  run under an agent's Bash tool, so what it prints reaches a tool
  result: the owner accepts that risk by granting a set.
- Agents are never resumed automatically (a resume costs money). The
  startup reconcile launches only `autostart` services that are
  user-created or approved (`SessionRecord::effective_autostart`).
- Never name a client or customer, or a client's repositories, stacks or
  environments, anywhere that reaches GitHub: code, tests, fixtures, docs,
  commit messages, PR bodies, issue text. Say "the client project" or "a
  pipeline". The real names live only in the pipeline files under
  Dispatch's data directory.

## Architecture

The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall
  clock. Time comes in through `Clock`. Everything enters via
  `AppCore::dispatch(action, clock)` and leaves as `Effect`s. Startup is a
  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every
  change to a workspace emits `Effect::Save`.
- `src/ports/` holds traits for outside capabilities. `src/adapters/`
  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on
  private sockets.
- `src/app.rs` owns core plus adapters. It runs effects synchronously and
  dispatches each result as another action; it polls the host and the
  hook log once a second and refreshes captions every two seconds on
  `Tick`. Codex id discovery is a poll, not a thread.
- Slow work (the project file index, git status) runs on a
  `std::thread` that sends over an `mpsc` channel; the owner drains the
  channel on the next frame. Anything the core needs to know still
  enters as one action.
- `src/ui/` only draws. `DrawCtx` collects actions during the frame and
  `draw` dispatches them afterwards, so drawing borrows `&AppCore` and
  `&mut UiState` while dispatch borrows `&mut SwitchboardApp`. `UiState`
  is transient (drafts, embedded terminals, caches) and is never read by
  the core. If logic appears under `ui/`, move it to the core.

Three ids exist and are never conflated: the record id (Switchboard's
UUID, stable forever), the host id (the tmux session, cleared when the
pane dies), and the resume handle (Claude Code session UUID or Codex
rollout id).

## Extending the contract

- `src/core/model.rs`, `src/core/action.rs` (`AppAction`/`Effect`), and
  `src/ports/` are the shared contract. Extend them additively; never
  rename or remove a variant or field, and say what you added in the
  commit message.
- A change to any type in `model.rs` that is serialized needs a
  `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Readers
  accept older versions; the store refuses to write a newer one.
- Writes to records go through the store's atomic path (temp file,
  fsync, `.bak`, rename). Never write a record file any other way.

## Adding a feature

1. Action variant plus core transition plus a core test in
   `src/core/tests.rs`.
2. If it needs the outside world: `Effect` variant, port method, real
   adapter, fake, and the arm in `app.rs` that runs it.
3. Widget under `src/ui/` and a UI test in `tests/ui.rs`.
4. A `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line in `src/script.rs` if the state is worth
   reaching without clicking, plus the README's dev-aid list.
5. README Layout table for any new file; design.md status section for
   any milestone item.

## Driving the live app

There is no keystroke injection. Put the running app into a state with
`SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT=<file>` (one action per line, see `src/script.rs`)
while `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` and `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` point at test
locations, then screenshot the window with `screencapture -l <window
id>`. Keep the data dir path short: the wake socket path has a 104-byte
limit. Hook events can be injected by running `switchboard-hook <EventName>`
by hand with the hook JSON on stdin and `SWITCHBOARD_RECORD_ID` and
`SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` set, for example
`echo '{"error":"rate_limit"}' | switchboard-hook StopFailure` or
`echo '{"tool_name":"AskUserQuestion"}' | switchboard-hook PermissionRequest`.

## Testing rules

- Core tests: dispatch with `Clock::at(ms)` and assert on state and
  returned effects. Never sleep.
- UI tests (`tests/ui.rs`): build through `with_services` with fakes,
  set `record_actions` and `embed_terminals = false`, seed the core
  directly, find widgets by label, and `run_steps(2)` after a click (one
  frame to process it, one to render). `type_text` only sends a Text
  event; call `.focus()` on the node first. Size the harness tall enough
  that everything you click is on screen. Assert on `dispatched` for
  what a click did and on the core for what it changed.
- tmux integration tests live beside the tmux adapter and in
  `tests/gate.rs`. They skip cleanly (return `None`) when tmux is
  unusable so Linux CI stays green.
- Tests that spend money or open windows are `#[ignore]`d in
  `tests/live.rs` and the agent items of `tests/gate.rs`, with the exact
  command to run each in the file's doc comment. Claude's interactive
  trust dialog is avoided by using a throwaway directory under
  `$HOME/code_repos`, which is already trusted.

## egui / eframe 0.36 gotchas

Much online material shows the pre-0.36 API and does not compile. When an
API does not match expectations, read the crate source under
`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/egui-0.36*` rather than guessing.

- `eframe::App` is `fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, frame)`, not
  `update(&mut self, ctx, frame)`. Get the context with `ui.ctx()`.
- Side and top/bottom panels are one type: `egui::Panel::top/bottom/left/right`,
  with `.exact_size(..)` and `.resizable(false)`. Panels take `.show(ui, ..)`.
- `egui_kittest`: `Harness::builder().with_size(..).build_eframe(|cc| ..)`.
  Import `Role` from `egui::accesskit`.
- Use `GAP` and `PAD` from `ui/mod.rs` for spacing so views line up.
- `CollapsingHeader::id_salt(x)` hashes `x` into an `IdSalt` first, so
  `ui.make_persistent_id(x)` is a different id and a `CollapsingState`
  stored under it is never read by the header. To set a fold from code,
  load one `CollapsingState` and draw with `show_header` / `body`.

## Platform-specific code

The crate forbids `unsafe`. Native calls (AppKit via `objc2`,
`security-framework`) go in a small adapter behind
`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` using safe wrapper crates. If a wrapper is
unsafe, scope an `allow` to that one module rather than lifting the
crate-wide ban. macOS-only dependencies go in the
`[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]` table.

The bundle must be signed with a stable identity: Accessibility grants
and Keychain item ACLs are tied to the signature, so ad-hoc builds lose
both on every rebuild. `scripts/bundle.sh` has the recipe.

CI runs clippy on Linux, and a `cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))` arm is
never compiled here. For the dispatch crate, check it before pushing:

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu   # once
cargo clippy --locked -p dispatch --all-targets --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- -D warnings
```

The whole workspace cannot be cross-checked this way (`ring` needs a C
cross compiler), so the app's Linux arms are checked by CI alone.

## Style

- Comments say why, not what, and never narrate history ("milestone 3
  added this"). Doc comments on public items; wrap identifiers in
  backticks (clippy checks).
- Prefer simple idiomatic code over clever code. Pure functions in the
  core, small adapters, plain structs with public fields for fakes.
- Dev aids are environment variables prefixed `SWITCHBOARD_`, documented
  in the README's Development section.
- Local secrets for development live in `.env`, which is git-ignored.
  Never print them.

## Working with the user

The user is learning Rust. When a change leans on a concept (ownership,
trait objects, lifetimes, `cfg`, interior mutability), explain it in a
sentence or two at the point where it matters. Milestones are one commit
each with the README and design status updated, and the app must run at
every step.

Issue #230: A web control surface: the remote port serves a browser page, paired from a URL that carries the code

## What I want

A second control surface beside the headset app: a page the host serves itself, opened in any browser on the local network (a phone, an iPad, another Mac), that lists the sessions with the waiting ones marked, shows a session's last response or screen, and sends a reply. It runs over the remote port that already exists. Nothing to install on the device, no App Store, no Xcode.

## What exists

- The remote port (`docs/remote-client.md`; `src/adapters/remote.rs`; `serve_remote` in `src/app.rs`): TLS with a per-installation self-signed certificate, pairing by a code with a pinned key, bearer tokens, the `/api/v1/*` read and control endpoints, the `/api/v1/events` WebSocket with the revision counter and `changed` events, redaction before every cut. Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused.
- The pairing window (`src/ui/remote.rs`): a QR carrying `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}` as JSON, the same in text beside it, open for five minutes or three wrong codes. The headset pairs from the Bonjour record and a typed code; the command-line `switchboard-remote pair` takes the QR's text as one argument.
- Three speakers of the protocol already: the visionOS app, `switchboard-remote`, and the fixtures shared by `tests/remote.rs` and the Swift tests.

## The shape

- **The host serves the page from the same port.** `GET /` and the page's few files answer with HTML, CSS and JS embedded in the binary at compile time (`include_str!`), so there is no build step, no bundler and no package manager. Same origin as the API: the page calls `/api/v1/...` and opens `/api/v1/events` directly.
- **The page speaks the protocol the headset speaks.** REST for reads and commands, the events socket for live changes, replies applied by revision the way §4.4 says. No new read model unless the page cannot do without one.
- **Pairing from a URL.** The pairing window's QR becomes a URL, `https://<address>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`, so a phone's camera opens it in the browser. The page reads the query, removes it from the address bar with `history.replaceState` before anything else happens, compares the key in the URL with the one `/info` presents, posts `/api/v1/pair` only when they match, keeps the token, and shows the sessions. The code never stays in the address bar or the history. The native text path (`switchboard-remote pair`, the headset's paste) takes the URL too, or the JSON as before.
- **The first cut of the page.** Sessions grouped by project, waiting ones first and marked, each with its kind, state and the one-line excerpt the card shows; a session view with the last response for a Claude Code session or the screen for anything else, refreshed on `changed`; a reply box that posts `send` when the device has `control` scope and is hidden otherwise; the device's scope and host name in the header; "identity changed, pair again" and "revoked" states said plainly.

## Decisions the plan must settle

1. **Browser trust in the self-signed certificate.** The native client pins the SPKI; a browser cannot. The first visit shows a certificate warning the owner clicks through, and the browser then trusts that certificate for that address. The plan says what this buys and what it does not: the `key` in the URL lets a genuine page refuse to send the code to a host whose `/info` key differs, but a page served by an impostor is not a genuine page. Either the click-through on the local network is the trust step, said in the paired-devices dialog, or the host offers its certificate for download so the owner can trust it on the device first. Pick one, say why, and keep §5's rule that no non-loopback bind serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and now the page itself before pairing.
2. **How the token reaches the WebSocket.** A browser cannot set a header on `new WebSocket()`, and the spec forbids the token in a URL. Candidates: the `/pair` reply sets an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie that `fetch` and the WebSocket both carry and the page's script never sees, or the token travels as a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value. The host keeps accepting the bearer header for the native clients. The choice also decides where the token lives on the device; `localStorage` is readable by any script on the origin, a cookie is not.
3. **One QR or two.** One URL read by the browser and by the native text path is the preference; the headset has no camera and the CLI parses text, so the JSON form can be kept only if something still needs it.
4. **Static paths on a port whose allowlist is `/api/v1/*`.** The exact set of paths, their `Content-Type`, a `Content-Security-Policy` with no inline script and no external resource, no caching across versions, which pool and rate window an unpaired browser's page load counts against (§4.1 allows four unauthenticated connections), and what the page shows when opened without a code and without a token.
5. **Where the page lives and how it is tested.** `web/` embedded at compile time; a test in `tests/remote.rs` that the embedded page references only paths the host serves and that the new paths answer with the headers the plan names; the pairing flow tested end to end with the host's own HTTP client as the CLI does, since no UI test drives a browser; the fixture set extended if a view changes.
6. **The device record.** A browser is a paired device like any other: a name from the user agent (`Safari on iPhone`), scope chosen in the pairing window as today, listed and revocable in the paired-devices dialog.

## Not in this cut

- Dispatch tickets and decisions on the page (the API serves them; a later issue).
- The conversation beyond the last response, drafts, dictation, runs and pinned files (the API serves them; later).
- Anything beyond the local network: no relay, no tunnel; §9 of the spec stands.

44	| Docs to amend | `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1, §4.3, §5, §11, §13; `docs/design.md` remote status (`:3107`); `README.md` Layout (src/adapters/remote.rs row, tests/remote.rs row, new `web/` row); `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased |
45	| No `web/` directory exists yet | |
46	
47	## 3. Findings that change the plan
48	
49	1. **The certificate has no subject alternative name.** `CertificateParams::new(Vec::new())` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:99`). Native clients pin the SPKI and ignore names. Browsers validate the name against the host in the URL (an IP such as `192.168.x.y`, or `localhost`). With no SAN every browser reports a *name mismatch* as well as "self-signed", and iOS Safari's click-through for it is flakier. This needs fixing for the feature (and it is additive, because the SPKI is unchanged): add IP and DNS SANs, which means the cert must be **reissued from the same key** on address change. The spec already says (§5) a reissue from the same key keeps pins valid, but `identity.json` currently stores one certificate made once. Settle: SANs for the current LAN addresses + `localhost` + `<hostname>.local`, reissued from the stored key when the address set changes (key is in the Keychain; `make_identity` generates both together today, so a "reissue cert from key" function is new). Also rcgen's default validity is very long; iOS only honours "trust this certificate" profiles for ≤398 days, so if decision 1 picks certificate download, validity and `serverAuth` EKU must be set explicitly. This is the main hidden cost of the issue.
50	2. **There is no clean way to pin in a browser. State it plainly (decision 1).** Recommendation: **the click-through is the trust step, said in the paired-devices dialog; do not offer a certificate download in this cut.**
51	   - Why: a download means a configuration profile on iOS and a Keychain import on macOS: it makes the owner install a root-trust-adjacent artifact on a phone, which is more dangerous than the problem, needs the 398-day/EKU/SAN work above, and has to be served by the same unauthenticated port.
52	   - What the click-through buys: the browser remembers the exception for that origin and the channel is encrypted to whoever answered. What it does not buy: authenticity of the first page. The `key` in the URL protects against an impostor `/info`, but an impostor serving the page can omit the check and read the code. Say this in the dialog sentence. The QR is out of band, so the real protection is that the code is 40 bits, single-use, three attempts globally (§5), and only the owner's screen shows it.
53	   - A compensating step worth the plan's attention: show the key's short form (`short_hash`, `src/ui/remote.rs:303`) **on the page** after pairing and in the paired-devices row, so the owner can compare by eye as the headset flow does.
54	3. **Token transport (decision 2): recommend the cookie.** Reasons: `fetch` and `new WebSocket` both send it without script access; `localStorage` is readable by any script on the origin; the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` route needs the token in script memory and in a header that proxies/log lines see, and the host would have to echo the subprotocol. Costs the plan must include:
55	   - `RemoteRequest` gains `cookie` (take only the `sb_token`-named cookie out of the headers, as the bearer is taken out so it is "never logged with them", `src/adapters/remote.rs:355-358`); `authenticate` reads bearer, else cookie. Additive.
56	   - `RemoteReply` needs a way to add a `Set-Cookie` header on the `/pair` reply and to set a content type/headers for static files. `respond` (`:530`) hard-codes the head; change `RemoteReply` additively (a `headers: Vec<(&'static str,String)>` or a `content_type` plus extras) with `Default`-style helpers so the ~40 constructors in `app.rs` keep compiling. Check how many sites build `RemoteReply { .. }` literally (many: `app.rs:1675`, `:1684`, `:3570` and others) before choosing. A constructor-based or `..Default` change is cheaper.
57	   - **Cookie auth opens CSRF and cross-site WebSocket hijack that bearer headers never had.** `SameSite=Strict` covers most, but a LAN page on another origin at the *same host different port* is same-site. Require on every cookie-authenticated request that mutates, and on the WebSocket upgrade: `Origin` equals `https://<Host header>`. That means parsing `origin` and `host` too. Bearer-header requests skip the check. `Secure` works on an untrusted self-signed origin once the exception is accepted. Add the `Path=/`, and `Max-Age` long (the token does not expire; revocation is the control).
58	   - Cookies are per host, not per port (browsers ignore the port for cookie scoping): two Switchboard hosts on one machine/IP with different ports would **overwrite each other's cookie**. Name the cookie with the port or the first 8 chars of the `server_id` (`sb_<id8>`), or accept one-host-per-address and say so. Recommend the id-suffixed name; it also makes "identity changed" detectable.
59	   - The pairing reply must keep returning the token in the JSON body for native clients (do not change the body), and *also* set the cookie, only when the request carries a marker (e.g. an `X-Switchboard-Web: 1` header or `"web": true` in the body) so the CLI does not receive cookies.
60	4. **The "one-line excerpt the card shows" is not on the wire.** `last_message` lives on the record from the Stop hook (`src/adapters/hooks.rs:71`, `src/bin/switchboard-hook.rs:37`); `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has no such field and `docs/remote-client.md` §4.3 says the card excerpt is the record's `last_message`, "a field of the session's metadata". Either add an additive, redacted, 4 KiB-bounded `last_message` (or `excerpt`) to `SessionView`, which then flows through the fingerprint (`src/core/revision.rs`) and the Swift fixtures (decoding must stay tolerant: the Swift side decodes with defaults for new fields, check `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Views.swift`), or the page shows state + `waiting_reason` only and fetches `last-response` on open. The issue says "no new read model unless the page cannot do without one"; I'd say the card excerpt is that case, and the plan should do it through the redaction path (§4.3: card excerpt "masked from the turn's full text, then cut"). Confirm with `rg last_message src/app.rs` — it is not served today.
61	5. **Pool accounting for a browser page load (decision 4).** A browser opens up to 6 parallel connections per origin, each is an unauthenticated connection until its first reply with `authenticated: true`. The static files return `authenticated: false` forever, so a connection that only serves page files stays in the pool of 4 and a 5th simultaneous connection is closed at accept. With HTTP/1.1 keep-alive the page, CSS and JS share connections, but Chrome speculatively opens extra ones. Plan: (a) serve the page from a small number of files (`/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css`, maybe one favicon response) and put CSS+JS inline-free but few; (b) the page's own `fetch` carrying the cookie will make a connection move to the paired pool on its first authenticated reply, which already works; (c) the static route needs its own rate window (it is not covered by `Limits::limited`, `:631`): e.g. 120/minute per listener, counted in the connection thread, answered 429 before the frame. Static bytes should be answered **on the connection thread, not the frame**: they are `&'static str`, need no core state, and would otherwise occupy the 64-slot inbox and the 8-per-pass drain. The one wrinkle is that `serve_remote` is where the allowlist lives today; the new allowlist for static paths would live in the adapter (`connection`), which §4.1 says must be "thin"; keep it to an exact-match table, fixed at compile time. This also keeps §5's "nothing before pairing but `/info`, `/pair` and now the page itself" true by construction: the static table is closed and contains no host data.
62	6. **Allowlist change in the spec.** "Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" (`src/app.rs:3023`, spec §4.3 "refused before translation") becomes: exact `GET` of `/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css` (and optional `/favicon.ico` → 204/404) served; every other non-`/api/v1/` path remains 404. Methods other than GET/HEAD on those → 405 (`405` already in the reason table). `GET /` with the pairing query is the same document.
63	7. **Headers for the static answers (decision 4).** Proposed set, all tested in `tests/remote.rs`:
64	   - `/`: `text/html; charset=utf-8`; `/app.js`: `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`; `/app.css`: `text/css; charset=utf-8`.
65	   - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'` covers `wss:` same-origin in current browsers; Safari older than 15.4 did not match `'self'` for WebSocket, so add `wss:` explicitly if testing shows it (cannot be tested without a browser: note as a known risk).
66	   - `Cache-Control: no-store` (the page carries no secrets, but "no caching across versions" in the issue; an `ETag` of the build version is the alternative and also fine, but `no-store` is simplest and the files are small). `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (the URL briefly carries the code), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.
67	   - The pairing URL query reaches the server in the request line; it is parsed into `RemoteRequest.query` and the code must **not** be logged: `refuse`/log lines print `request.path` only (no query) already (`src/app.rs:3760`), keep it so. The page script strips it with `history.replaceState` first. `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` stops it leaking via referrer; the history entry is replaced before any navigation.
68	   - Also make the code in the URL harmless after the fact: it is single-use and closes the window on success, which is already true.
69	8. **Version skew between page and host:** page is `include_str!`ed so it always matches the binary; the page should read `protocol` from `/info` (`REMOTE_PROTOCOL`) and refuse a higher major, as the Swift client does.
70	9. **URL form for the QR (decision 3): one URL, keep the JSON as parse-only compatibility.** `https://<address>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`. Everything is URL-safe (Crockford code, hex key, UUID). Changes: `src/ui/remote.rs:160` builds the URL (needs a non-empty address; when `local_address()` is `None` fall back to the JSON/no QR, since the URL needs a host); "Copy invite" copies the URL; the multiple `addresses` in the JSON collapse to one, so choose the address a phone can reach (`remote::local_address()`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:962`). `PairingInvite.parse` (Swift) and the CLI must accept both: if the text starts with `https://`, parse host:port and the three query items, else JSON. Keep JSON decoding for old hosts ↔ new clients (a new client against an old host's pasted JSON; an old CLI cannot read the new URL, which is the one forward-compat break to say in the changelog). Add a Swift fixture and a parse test, and a Rust test that the UI payload parses. The headset's typed-code path and Bonjour path need no change. There is no reason to keep two QRs.
71	10. **Revocation visibility.** Revoke drops the subscriber queue so the socket closes (`src/app.rs:486`); the page then re-requests, gets 401 `unauthorized`, and shows "revoked". The page cannot tell "revoked" from "token never valid" except by having been paired earlier in this origin (cookie present at load, 401 on first call). Say "This device was revoked or the host forgot it. Pair again." Key rotation → new `spki_sha256` from `/info` ≠ remembered → "identity changed, pair again", and the page sends nothing.
72	11. **`/info` rate limit** (60/min per listener, `INFO_PER_MINUTE` `:584`) is shared by every browser load and by the page's reconnect loop. The page must call `/info` once per load, not per poll, and back off on 429.
73	12. **Reply by revision and the events socket from a browser.** Page needs: `hello` first; buffer events; snapshot; reconcile (§4.4). Browser `WebSocket` cannot set headers, so with the cookie it just connects to `wss://<host>/api/v1/events`. The frame sends `watch`/`unwatch` text frames the same as native. Subscriber `all` (scope=all) is not wanted: workers hidden.
74	13. **Waiting-first grouping needs only existing data:** `GET waiting` and `SessionView.waiting`, `card`, `kind`, `waiting_reason`. "A session that starts waiting moves to the top without a reload" = a `changed {waiting}` / `changed {session}` event, then refetch.
75	14. **Reply box:** posts `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` with an `op` (UUID via `crypto.randomUUID()`, which needs a secure context: fine under HTTPS even self-signed once excepted) and handles the three op statuses from `/ops/{op}` (§4.5): never resubmit on `interrupted`. Hidden unless the device's scope is `control`: scope is **not returned by any authenticated read today**. `/pair` returns it once; on a later load the page has only the cookie. Need a source: add an additive `scope` (and `device_name`) to an authenticated reply. Cheapest: a new `GET /api/v1/me` -> `{name, scope, server_name}` or extend `/info` with a `device` object when authenticated (`remote_info` is reached before `authenticate`, `src/app.rs:3028`, so `/info` would need to peek at the cookie/bearer). Prefer a new `GET /api/v1/device`, behind auth, read scope: one new arm in `serve_remote` plus the doc row. A scope lowered in the dialog (`SetDeviceScope`) then shows on the next call; the page should re-read it on a 403.
76	15. **Dispatch tickets / draft / dictation endpoints stay unused** (out of cut).
77	
78	## 4. Proposed shape (for the plan)
79	
80	Order, each a working app, smallest first (CLAUDE.md "Adding a feature" and one-commit milestones):
81	
82	1. **Cert SANs.** `make_identity`/reissue from the stored key; tests: SPKI unchanged across reissue; native pin still verifies; the cert lists the LAN IP and `localhost`. (`src/adapters/remote.rs`, `tests/remote.rs` `a_change_of_address_rebinds_the_port` `:1493` is the neighbor.)
83	2. **Adapter plumbing:** `RemoteRequest { cookie, origin, host }`, `RemoteReply` headers/content type, a closed static table answered in `connection` with its own rate window and pool behavior; `respond` takes headers. Unit tests in the adapter.
84	3. **Host API additions:** cookie auth in `authenticate`, `Set-Cookie` on a web `/pair`, Origin check for cookie-authenticated POST/upgrade, `GET /api/v1/device`, excerpt on `SessionView` (control crate additive) with fingerprint and fixtures. Core test where state moves (none expected: no new core state).
85	4. **`web/` (index.html, app.js, app.css)** embedded with `include_str!`; no build step. `web/` row in README Layout. Plain JS, no inline script (CSP).
86	5. **QR becomes the URL**; Swift `PairingInvite.parse` and CLI accept URL or JSON; script/dev-aid unchanged except README note on "Copy invite".
87	6. **Docs:** remote-client.md §4.1 (static pool), §4.3 (static paths table and `device`), §5 (cookie, Origin, click-through, key on page, URL form, dialog sentence), §11 tests, §13 decisions; design.md remote status; CHANGELOG Unreleased line; the paired-devices dialog sentence in `src/ui/remote.rs`.
88	
89	## 5. Tests (decision 5)
90	
91	- `tests/remote.rs`, over the real TLS listener with the existing `http` helper (`:245`; it must be extended to return headers, today it returns status + body only):
92	  - Each static path answers 200 with its Content-Type, CSP, `no-store`, `nosniff`; unknown non-`/api/v1/` path 404; POST to `/` 405; `HEAD` handled or refused consistently.
93	  - **Embedded-page consistency:** scan `web/index.html` and `web/app.js` for `src=`, `href=`, and `fetch(`/`WebSocket(` string literals; every one is either a served static path or begins `/api/v1/` and matches a route in the allowlist (assert against a list exported from the adapter, not a hand-copy). No `http://`/`https://` externals, no `<script>` without `src`, no inline `on*=` handlers or `style=` (CSP).
94	  - Pairing end-to-end with the host's own HTTP client as the CLI does: open window, GET `/?code=...` (200, static), GET `/api/v1/info`, check key equality, POST `/pair` with the web marker, assert `Set-Cookie` has `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`, then GET `/api/v1/waiting` using only the cookie; assert JSON body of `/pair` still has the token for the non-web path and **no** cookie there.
95	  - Cookie auth: Origin mismatch refused on POST `send` and on the upgrade; no Origin with bearer allowed; cookie from the wrong `server_id` suffix ignored; revoke → next cookie request 401; lowered scope → `send` refused 403 with the `control` scope message.
96	  - Static paths do not consume the frame inbox (flood 200 `GET /` and assert a paired metadata request is still answered in a pass) and respect the new rate window; unauthenticated pool of 4 unaffected for paired clients (existing stalled-strangers test pattern).
97	  - The pairing URL parse: a Rust unit test in `src/ui/remote.rs` that the payload is a URL whose three query items round-trip; Swift test for URL and JSON invite; a fixture in `client/Fixtures`.
98	- No test drives a browser (as the issue says). The `history.replaceState`-first ordering and the key comparison are JS that cannot be tested in CI here; state that, keep `app.js` small with these two lines first, and do one manual run per CLAUDE.md "Driving the live app" with `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR`/`SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` on test locations and screenshot a headless browser if any is available.
99	
100	## 6. Risks and open questions for the owner
101	
102	- Certificate SANs and browser acceptance on iOS Safari cannot be verified from CI. The plan should list a manual acceptance on a real phone (the issue's acceptance paragraph).
103	- Cookie `Secure` over a self-signed exception works in Safari/Chrome; Firefox is stricter about exceptions per origin with a changed SAN set. Reissuing the cert when the address changes invalidates the browser's saved exception: the owner clicks through again (not a pairing loss, since the key is the same and the cookie stays).
104	- The URL puts the code in the request line the host receives (and in the QR image). The host logs path only. Browser history: removed by `replaceState`, but the initial navigation entry is already recorded by some browsers before script runs; mitigate with the single-use code and 5-minute window, and say so.
105	- Mixed content: the page is `https`, so the QR must be `https://`. Phones that scan and offer "open in browser" may preview the URL (some scanners fetch it server-side; here it is a LAN address so they cannot).
106	- Multi-host on one IP and cookie scoping (finding 3).
107	- Is the Bonjour-name (`<hostname>.local`) wanted as a second address in the SANs? Not required for the first cut.
108	- Whether to extend `SessionView` with the excerpt (finding 4) or drop the excerpt for the first cut. Recommendation: add it (additive, redacted).
109	
110	## 7. Not touched / confirmed constraints
111	
112	- No change to `model.rs` (no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump), no new on-disk file, no new dependency for the page; maybe none for the host (cookie and header parsing by hand in the existing reader).
113	- Hard rules respected by the plan: nothing written into project dirs; no secrets in the URL beyond the single-use code; no `~/.claude/settings.json` change; no client names anywhere.
114	- Commit hygiene reminder for the implementer: no tool attribution lines in commits or PR bodies (CLAUDE.md overrides the harness reminder), check the body for `claude.ai` before `gh pr create`.

# Issue #230 — web control surface on the remote port: investigation notes

Read: CLAUDE.md, docs/lessons.md, docs/remote-client.md (all of it), design.md's
remote client section (starts `docs/design.md:3107`), and the code below. Nothing was written
except this file. Line numbers are from this worktree (branch
`dispatch/230-a-web-control-surface-the-remote-port-se`, at Release 0.4.1).

## 1. On-disk record and rehydration (before any pane)

The page is a **new client of existing records; it adds almost nothing to disk.**

- Host side, durable, already present:
  - `<data dir>/identity.json` (server id, certificate, `spki_sha256`, listen preference; `src/ports/remote.rs:26`), key in the Keychain.
  - `<data dir>/devices.json`: `PairedDevice { id, name, scope, token_sha256, created, last_seen }` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`). A browser is one more row. Issue decision 6 needs **no schema change**: `name` is already a free string. The one new input is the device name from the `User-Agent` (parsed to `Safari on iPhone`), which `/pair` currently takes from the body's `device_name` (`src/app.rs:3650`). Simplest: the page computes the name and posts it as `device_name` (no host change). A header parse on the host is not needed. Cap/sanitize the length anyway.
  - If cookies are chosen (decision 2), the host still stores only the token's SHA-256. **Do not add a session table.** The cookie value is the bearer token itself, so `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) looks it up by `token_sha256` exactly as now. Revocation (`AppAction::RevokeDevice`, `src/core/remote.rs:86`) therefore already kills it on the next request, with no new record.
- Page side, durable: one thing, the token. Under the cookie option it is in an `HttpOnly` cookie the script never reads, so the page keeps **no durable state of its own**. Everything else (sessions, last responses, screens) is in memory and refetched, which is the rule the spec gives clients (§7: bodies in memory only). Scope/host name come from `/info` and an authenticated read.
- Rehydration on page load, no pairing query present:
  1. `GET /api/v1/info` → `server_id`, `spki_sha256`, `server_name`, `epoch`, `revision`.
  2. Authenticated `GET /api/v1/projects`, per project `GET .../sessions` (or `waiting`), carrying the cookie.
  3. 401 → "pair again" state. A key differing from the one remembered → "identity changed". Revoked → 401 with `unauthorized` ("the token is not known; pair again", `src/app.rs:3142`), which the page must show as "revoked", not as a generic error.
  4. Open `/api/v1/events` (subscribe first), then snapshot, then reconcile by revision (§4.4), and `watch` the open session's `conversation` or `screen`.
- Bearer-header clients (visionOS, CLI) keep working untouched. Nothing here changes `SCHEMA_VERSION` or `model.rs`.
- What the page remembers across a reload besides the cookie: at most the host's `server_id` + `spki_sha256` in `localStorage` (per-viewer convenience, tolerated empty), so "identity changed" can be said. The spec says the client keeps the pin; a browser cannot enforce it at the TLS layer (see §3), so this is advisory only.

## 2. Where the code is (files:lines)

| Concern | Where |
|---|---|
| Request parse; headers lowercased into a local vec, only `content-length`, `authorization`, `upgrade`/`sec-websocket-key` kept | `src/adapters/remote.rs:444-514` (`read_request`). No `cookie`, `origin`, `host`, `user-agent` field exists on `RemoteRequest` (`:360-372`). |
| Response writer: **always** `Content-Type: application/json`, fixed headers, no way to add headers or another type | `respond` `src/adapters/remote.rs:530-553`; status reason table has no 304/302/405-specific others |
| Pools (4 unauth / 12 paired), rate windows keyed by exact path (`PAIR_PATH`, `INFO_PATH`) | `:567-640`; `Limits::limited` `:631` returns false for any other path |
| Connection loop; a connection joins the paired pool on its first reply with `authenticated: true` | `connection` `src/adapters/remote.rs:770-875` |
| Frame routing: everything outside `/api/v1/` is 404 here | `serve_remote` `src/app.rs:3017-3024`; match arms `:3044-3117` |
| Bearer auth | `authenticate` `src/app.rs:3127-3152` (bearer only) |
| Events socket: auth then `remote_subscribe`; revocation drops the queue → socket closes | `src/app.rs:3036`, `:2723-2760`, revoke at `:486-497` |
| `/info` (capabilities list, `spki_sha256`, `pairing_open`) | `remote_info` `src/app.rs:3568-3599` |
| `/pair`: checks window, `spki_sha256`, code; counts failures; mints token; reply is JSON with `token` | `remote_pair` `src/app.rs:3606-3673` |
| Envelope `{epoch, revision, body}`; refusals | `envelope` `:3730`, `refuse` `:3754` |
| Pairing window UI and the QR payload (JSON `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`) | `src/ui/remote.rs:140-215`; payload built `:160-167`; QR from `qr_texture` `:280`; "Copy invite" `:197-206`; redaction sentence `:72` |
| Pairing state | `src/core/remote.rs` (window, code, failures; `RevokeDevice` `:86`, `SetDeviceScope` `:96`) |
| Cert/identity: `make_identity` makes a cert with **empty SAN list** and CN `Switchboard <id>` | `src/adapters/remote.rs:95-126` |
| Native text pairing: `PairingInvite.parse` decodes JSON only | `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:90-120`; CLI `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:107-125` (one arg = invite, or `host:port code key`) |
| Fixtures / tests that must stay green | `tests/remote.rs` (`http` helper `:245`, `pair` `:406`, allowlist test `:682`, fixtures `:1587`, `:1828`; subscribe helper `:1960`); `client/Fixtures` |
| Docs to amend | `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1, §4.3, §5, §11, §13; `docs/design.md` remote status (`:3107`); `README.md` Layout (src/adapters/remote.rs row, tests/remote.rs row, new `web/` row); `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased |
| No `web/` directory exists yet | |

## 3. Findings that change the plan

1. **The certificate has no subject alternative name.** `CertificateParams::new(Vec::new())` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:99`). Native clients pin the SPKI and ignore names. Browsers validate the name against the host in the URL (an IP such as `192.168.x.y`, or `localhost`). With no SAN every browser reports a *name mismatch* as well as "self-signed", and iOS Safari's click-through for it is flakier. This needs fixing for the feature (and it is additive, because the SPKI is unchanged): add IP and DNS SANs, which means the cert must be **reissued from the same key** on address change. The spec already says (§5) a reissue from the same key keeps pins valid, but `identity.json` currently stores one certificate made once. Settle: SANs for the current LAN addresses + `localhost` + `<hostname>.local`, reissued from the stored key when the address set changes (key is in the Keychain; `make_identity` generates both together today, so a "reissue cert from key" function is new). Also rcgen's default validity is very long; iOS only honours "trust this certificate" profiles for ≤398 days, so if decision 1 picks certificate download, validity and `serverAuth` EKU must be set explicitly. This is the main hidden cost of the issue.
2. **There is no clean way to pin in a browser. State it plainly (decision 1).** Recommendation: **the click-through is the trust step, said in the paired-devices dialog; do not offer a certificate download in this cut.**
   - Why: a download means a configuration profile on iOS and a Keychain import on macOS: it makes the owner install a root-trust-adjacent artifact on a phone, which is more dangerous than the problem, needs the 398-day/EKU/SAN work above, and has to be served by the same unauthenticated port.
   - What the click-through buys: the browser remembers the exception for that origin and the channel is encrypted to whoever answered. What it does not buy: authenticity of the first page. The `key` in the URL protects against an impostor `/info`, but an impostor serving the page can omit the check and read the code. Say this in the dialog sentence. The QR is out of band, so the real protection is that the code is 40 bits, single-use, three attempts globally (§5), and only the owner's screen shows it.
   - A compensating step worth the plan's attention: show the key's short form (`short_hash`, `src/ui/remote.rs:303`) **on the page** after pairing and in the paired-devices row, so the owner can compare by eye as the headset flow does.
3. **Token transport (decision 2): recommend the cookie.** Reasons: `fetch` and `new WebSocket` both send it without script access; `localStorage` is readable by any script on the origin; the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` route needs the token in script memory and in a header that proxies/log lines see, and the host would have to echo the subprotocol. Costs the plan must include:
   - `RemoteRequest` gains `cookie` (take only the `sb_token`-named cookie out of the headers, as the bearer is taken out so it is "never logged with them", `src/adapters/remote.rs:355-358`); `authenticate` reads bearer, else cookie. Additive.
   - `RemoteReply` needs a way to add a `Set-Cookie` header on the `/pair` reply and to set a content type/headers for static files. `respond` (`:530`) hard-codes the head; change `RemoteReply` additively (a `headers: Vec<(&'static str,String)>` or a `content_type` plus extras) with `Default`-style helpers so the ~40 constructors in `app.rs` keep compiling. Check how many sites build `RemoteReply { .. }` literally (many: `app.rs:1675`, `:1684`, `:3570` and others) before choosing. A constructor-based or `..Default` change is cheaper.
   - **Cookie auth opens CSRF and cross-site WebSocket hijack that bearer headers never had.** `SameSite=Strict` covers most, but a LAN page on another origin at the *same host different port* is same-site. Require on every cookie-authenticated request that mutates, and on the WebSocket upgrade: `Origin` equals `https://<Host header>`. That means parsing `origin` and `host` too. Bearer-header requests skip the check. `Secure` works on an untrusted self-signed origin once the exception is accepted. Add the `Path=/`, and `Max-Age` long (the token does not expire; revocation is the control).
   - Cookies are per host, not per port (browsers ignore the port for cookie scoping): two Switchboard hosts on one machine/IP with different ports would **overwrite each other's cookie**. Name the cookie with the port or the first 8 chars of the `server_id` (`sb_<id8>`), or accept one-host-per-address and say so. Recommend the id-suffixed name; it also makes "identity changed" detectable.
   - The pairing reply must keep returning the token in the JSON body for native clients (do not change the body), and *also* set the cookie, only when the request carries a marker (e.g. an `X-Switchboard-Web: 1` header or `"web": true` in the body) so the CLI does not receive cookies.
4. **The "one-line excerpt the card shows" is not on the wire.** `last_message` lives on the record from the Stop hook (`src/adapters/hooks.rs:71`, `src/bin/switchboard-hook.rs:37`); `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has no such field and `docs/remote-client.md` §4.3 says the card excerpt is the record's `last_message`, "a field of the session's metadata". Either add an additive, redacted, 4 KiB-bounded `last_message` (or `excerpt`) to `SessionView`, which then flows through the fingerprint (`src/core/revision.rs`) and the Swift fixtures (decoding must stay tolerant: the Swift side decodes with defaults for new fields, check `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Views.swift`), or the page shows state + `waiting_reason` only and fetches `last-response` on open. The issue says "no new read model unless the page cannot do without one"; I'd say the card excerpt is that case, and the plan should do it through the redaction path (§4.3: card excerpt "masked from the turn's full text, then cut"). Confirm with `rg last_message src/app.rs` — it is not served today.
5. **Pool accounting for a browser page load (decision 4).** A browser opens up to 6 parallel connections per origin, each is an unauthenticated connection until its first reply with `authenticated: true`. The static files return `authenticated: false` forever, so a connection that only serves page files stays in the pool of 4 and a 5th simultaneous connection is closed at accept. With HTTP/1.1 keep-alive the page, CSS and JS share connections, but Chrome speculatively opens extra ones. Plan: (a) serve the page from a small number of files (`/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css`, maybe one favicon response) and put CSS+JS inline-free but few; (b) the page's own `fetch` carrying the cookie will make a connection move to the paired pool on its first authenticated reply, which already works; (c) the static route needs its own rate window (it is not covered by `Limits::limited`, `:631`): e.g. 120/minute per listener, counted in the connection thread, answered 429 before the frame. Static bytes should be answered **on the connection thread, not the frame**: they are `&'static str`, need no core state, and would otherwise occupy the 64-slot inbox and the 8-per-pass drain. The one wrinkle is that `serve_remote` is where the allowlist lives today; the new allowlist for static paths would live in the adapter (`connection`), which §4.1 says must be "thin"; keep it to an exact-match table, fixed at compile time. This also keeps §5's "nothing before pairing but `/info`, `/pair` and now the page itself" true by construction: the static table is closed and contains no host data.
6. **Allowlist change in the spec.** "Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" (`src/app.rs:3023`, spec §4.3 "refused before translation") becomes: exact `GET` of `/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css` (and optional `/favicon.ico` → 204/404) served; every other non-`/api/v1/` path remains 404. Methods other than GET/HEAD on those → 405 (`405` already in the reason table). `GET /` with the pairing query is the same document.
7. **Headers for the static answers (decision 4).** Proposed set, all tested in `tests/remote.rs`:
   - `/`: `text/html; charset=utf-8`; `/app.js`: `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`; `/app.css`: `text/css; charset=utf-8`.
   - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'` covers `wss:` same-origin in current browsers; Safari older than 15.4 did not match `'self'` for WebSocket, so add `wss:` explicitly if testing shows it (cannot be tested without a browser: note as a known risk).
   - `Cache-Control: no-store` (the page carries no secrets, but "no caching across versions" in the issue; an `ETag` of the build version is the alternative and also fine, but `no-store` is simplest and the files are small). `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (the URL briefly carries the code), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.
   - The pairing URL query reaches the server in the request line; it is parsed into `RemoteRequest.query` and the code must **not** be logged: `refuse`/log lines print `request.path` only (no query) already (`src/app.rs:3760`), keep it so. The page script strips it with `history.replaceState` first. `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` stops it leaking via referrer; the history entry is replaced before any navigation.
   - Also make the code in the URL harmless after the fact: it is single-use and closes the window on success, which is already true.
8. **Version skew between page and host:** page is `include_str!`ed so it always matches the binary; the page should read `protocol` from `/info` (`REMOTE_PROTOCOL`) and refuse a higher major, as the Swift client does.
9. **URL form for the QR (decision 3): one URL, keep the JSON as parse-only compatibility.** `https://<address>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`. Everything is URL-safe (Crockford code, hex key, UUID). Changes: `src/ui/remote.rs:160` builds the URL (needs a non-empty address; when `local_address()` is `None` fall back to the JSON/no QR, since the URL needs a host); "Copy invite" copies the URL; the multiple `addresses` in the JSON collapse to one, so choose the address a phone can reach (`remote::local_address()`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:962`). `PairingInvite.parse` (Swift) and the CLI must accept both: if the text starts with `https://`, parse host:port and the three query items, else JSON. Keep JSON decoding for old hosts ↔ new clients (a new client against an old host's pasted JSON; an old CLI cannot read the new URL, which is the one forward-compat break to say in the changelog). Add a Swift fixture and a parse test, and a Rust test that the UI payload parses. The headset's typed-code path and Bonjour path need no change. There is no reason to keep two QRs.
10. **Revocation visibility.** Revoke drops the subscriber queue so the socket closes (`src/app.rs:486`); the page then re-requests, gets 401 `unauthorized`, and shows "revoked". The page cannot tell "revoked" from "token never valid" except by having been paired earlier in this origin (cookie present at load, 401 on first call). Say "This device was revoked or the host forgot it. Pair again." Key rotation → new `spki_sha256` from `/info` ≠ remembered → "identity changed, pair again", and the page sends nothing.
11. **`/info` rate limit** (60/min per listener, `INFO_PER_MINUTE` `:584`) is shared by every browser load and by the page's reconnect loop. The page must call `/info` once per load, not per poll, and back off on 429.
12. **Reply by revision and the events socket from a browser.** Page needs: `hello` first; buffer events; snapshot; reconcile (§4.4). Browser `WebSocket` cannot set headers, so with the cookie it just connects to `wss://<host>/api/v1/events`. The frame sends `watch`/`unwatch` text frames the same as native. Subscriber `all` (scope=all) is not wanted: workers hidden.
13. **Waiting-first grouping needs only existing data:** `GET waiting` and `SessionView.waiting`, `card`, `kind`, `waiting_reason`. "A session that starts waiting moves to the top without a reload" = a `changed {waiting}` / `changed {session}` event, then refetch.
14. **Reply box:** posts `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` with an `op` (UUID via `crypto.randomUUID()`, which needs a secure context: fine under HTTPS even self-signed once excepted) and handles the three op statuses from `/ops/{op}` (§4.5): never resubmit on `interrupted`. Hidden unless the device's scope is `control`: scope is **not returned by any authenticated read today**. `/pair` returns it once; on a later load the page has only the cookie. Need a source: add an additive `scope` (and `device_name`) to an authenticated reply. Cheapest: a new `GET /api/v1/me` -> `{name, scope, server_name}` or extend `/info` with a `device` object when authenticated (`remote_info` is reached before `authenticate`, `src/app.rs:3028`, so `/info` would need to peek at the cookie/bearer). Prefer a new `GET /api/v1/device`, behind auth, read scope: one new arm in `serve_remote` plus the doc row. A scope lowered in the dialog (`SetDeviceScope`) then shows on the next call; the page should re-read it on a 403.
15. **Dispatch tickets / draft / dictation endpoints stay unused** (out of cut).

## 4. Proposed shape (for the plan)

Order, each a working app, smallest first (CLAUDE.md "Adding a feature" and one-commit milestones):

1. **Cert SANs.** `make_identity`/reissue from the stored key; tests: SPKI unchanged across reissue; native pin still verifies; the cert lists the LAN IP and `localhost`. (`src/adapters/remote.rs`, `tests/remote.rs` `a_change_of_address_rebinds_the_port` `:1493` is the neighbor.)
2. **Adapter plumbing:** `RemoteRequest { cookie, origin, host }`, `RemoteReply` headers/content type, a closed static table answered in `connection` with its own rate window and pool behavior; `respond` takes headers. Unit tests in the adapter.
3. **Host API additions:** cookie auth in `authenticate`, `Set-Cookie` on a web `/pair`, Origin check for cookie-authenticated POST/upgrade, `GET /api/v1/device`, excerpt on `SessionView` (control crate additive) with fingerprint and fixtures. Core test where state moves (none expected: no new core state).
4. **`web/` (index.html, app.js, app.css)** embedded with `include_str!`; no build step. `web/` row in README Layout. Plain JS, no inline script (CSP).
5. **QR becomes the URL**; Swift `PairingInvite.parse` and CLI accept URL or JSON; script/dev-aid unchanged except README note on "Copy invite".
6. **Docs:** remote-client.md §4.1 (static pool), §4.3 (static paths table and `device`), §5 (cookie, Origin, click-through, key on page, URL form, dialog sentence), §11 tests, §13 decisions; design.md remote status; CHANGELOG Unreleased line; the paired-devices dialog sentence in `src/ui/remote.rs`.

## 5. Tests (decision 5)

- `tests/remote.rs`, over the real TLS listener with the existing `http` helper (`:245`; it must be extended to return headers, today it returns status + body only):
  - Each static path answers 200 with its Content-Type, CSP, `no-store`, `nosniff`; unknown non-`/api/v1/` path 404; POST to `/` 405; `HEAD` handled or refused consistently.
  - **Embedded-page consistency:** scan `web/index.html` and `web/app.js` for `src=`, `href=`, and `fetch(`/`WebSocket(` string literals; every one is either a served static path or begins `/api/v1/` and matches a route in the allowlist (assert against a list exported from the adapter, not a hand-copy). No `http://`/`https://` externals, no `<script>` without `src`, no inline `on*=` handlers or `style=` (CSP).
  - Pairing end-to-end with the host's own HTTP client as the CLI does: open window, GET `/?code=...` (200, static), GET `/api/v1/info`, check key equality, POST `/pair` with the web marker, assert `Set-Cookie` has `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`, then GET `/api/v1/waiting` using only the cookie; assert JSON body of `/pair` still has the token for the non-web path and **no** cookie there.
  - Cookie auth: Origin mismatch refused on POST `send` and on the upgrade; no Origin with bearer allowed; cookie from the wrong `server_id` suffix ignored; revoke → next cookie request 401; lowered scope → `send` refused 403 with the `control` scope message.
  - Static paths do not consume the frame inbox (flood 200 `GET /` and assert a paired metadata request is still answered in a pass) and respect the new rate window; unauthenticated pool of 4 unaffected for paired clients (existing stalled-strangers test pattern).
  - The pairing URL parse: a Rust unit test in `src/ui/remote.rs` that the payload is a URL whose three query items round-trip; Swift test for URL and JSON invite; a fixture in `client/Fixtures`.
- No test drives a browser (as the issue says). The `history.replaceState`-first ordering and the key comparison are JS that cannot be tested in CI here; state that, keep `app.js` small with these two lines first, and do one manual run per CLAUDE.md "Driving the live app" with `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR`/`SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` on test locations and screenshot a headless browser if any is available.

## 6. Risks and open questions for the owner

- Certificate SANs and browser acceptance on iOS Safari cannot be verified from CI. The plan should list a manual acceptance on a real phone (the issue's acceptance paragraph).
- Cookie `Secure` over a self-signed exception works in Safari/Chrome; Firefox is stricter about exceptions per origin with a changed SAN set. Reissuing the cert when the address changes invalidates the browser's saved exception: the owner clicks through again (not a pairing loss, since the key is the same and the cookie stays).
- The URL puts the code in the request line the host receives (and in the QR image). The host logs path only. Browser history: removed by `replaceState`, but the initial navigation entry is already recorded by some browsers before script runs; mitigate with the single-use code and 5-minute window, and say so.
- Mixed content: the page is `https`, so the QR must be `https://`. Phones that scan and offer "open in browser" may preview the URL (some scanners fetch it server-side; here it is a LAN address so they cannot).
- Multi-host on one IP and cookie scoping (finding 3).
- Is the Bonjour-name (`<hostname>.local`) wanted as a second address in the SANs? Not required for the first cut.
- Whether to extend `SessionView` with the excerpt (finding 4) or drop the excerpt for the first cut. Recommendation: add it (additive, redacted).

## 7. Not touched / confirmed constraints

- No change to `model.rs` (no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump), no new on-disk file, no new dependency for the page; maybe none for the host (cookie and header parsing by hand in the existing reader).
- Hard rules respected by the plan: nothing written into project dirs; no secrets in the URL beyond the single-use code; no `~/.claude/settings.json` change; no client names anywhere.
- Commit hygiene reminder for the implementer: no tool attribution lines in commits or PR bodies (CLAUDE.md overrides the harness reminder), check the body for `claude.ai` before `gh pr create`.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.
<total_tokens>15000000 tokens left</total_tokens>

WebSearch takes a `mode`. Use "standard" by default: it is the normal search, quick and cheap. Use "extended" only when a "standard" result comes back thin, off-target or possibly outdated, or from the start for hard-to-find or niche facts, very recent events, prices and availability, and multi-step research: it is thorough and fresh but several times the cost. When you plan several searches, send them in the same turn.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
