1	# Issue #230 — web control surface on the remote port: investigation notes
2	
3	Read: CLAUDE.md, docs/lessons.md, docs/remote-client.md (all of it), design.md's
4	remote client section (starts `docs/design.md:3107`), and the code below. Nothing was written
5	except this file. Line numbers are from this worktree (branch
6	`dispatch/230-a-web-control-surface-the-remote-port-se`, at Release 0.4.1).
7	
8	## 1. On-disk record and rehydration (before any pane)
9	
10	The page is a **new client of existing records; it adds almost nothing to disk.**
11	
12	- Host side, durable, already present:
13	  - `<data dir>/identity.json` (server id, certificate, `spki_sha256`, listen preference; `src/ports/remote.rs:26`), key in the Keychain.
14	  - `<data dir>/devices.json`: `PairedDevice { id, name, scope, token_sha256, created, last_seen }` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`). A browser is one more row. Issue decision 6 needs **no schema change**: `name` is already a free string. The one new input is the device name from the `User-Agent` (parsed to `Safari on iPhone`), which `/pair` currently takes from the body's `device_name` (`src/app.rs:3650`). Simplest: the page computes the name and posts it as `device_name` (no host change). A header parse on the host is not needed. Cap/sanitize the length anyway.
15	  - If cookies are chosen (decision 2), the host still stores only the token's SHA-256. **Do not add a session table.** The cookie value is the bearer token itself, so `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) looks it up by `token_sha256` exactly as now. Revocation (`AppAction::RevokeDevice`, `src/core/remote.rs:86`) therefore already kills it on the next request, with no new record.
16	- Page side, durable: one thing, the token. Under the cookie option it is in an `HttpOnly` cookie the script never reads, so the page keeps **no durable state of its own**. Everything else (sessions, last responses, screens) is in memory and refetched, which is the rule the spec gives clients (§7: bodies in memory only). Scope/host name come from `/info` and an authenticated read.
17	- Rehydration on page load, no pairing query present:
18	  1. `GET /api/v1/info` → `server_id`, `spki_sha256`, `server_name`, `epoch`, `revision`.
19	  2. Authenticated `GET /api/v1/projects`, per project `GET .../sessions` (or `waiting`), carrying the cookie.
20	  3. 401 → "pair again" state. A key differing from the one remembered → "identity changed". Revoked → 401 with `unauthorized` ("the token is not known; pair again", `src/app.rs:3142`), which the page must show as "revoked", not as a generic error.
21	  4. Open `/api/v1/events` (subscribe first), then snapshot, then reconcile by revision (§4.4), and `watch` the open session's `conversation` or `screen`.
22	- Bearer-header clients (visionOS, CLI) keep working untouched. Nothing here changes `SCHEMA_VERSION` or `model.rs`.
23	- What the page remembers across a reload besides the cookie: at most the host's `server_id` + `spki_sha256` in `localStorage` (per-viewer convenience, tolerated empty), so "identity changed" can be said. The spec says the client keeps the pin; a browser cannot enforce it at the TLS layer (see §3), so this is advisory only.
24	
25	## 2. Where the code is (files:lines)
26	
27	| Concern | Where |
28	|---|---|
29	| Request parse; headers lowercased into a local vec, only `content-length`, `authorization`, `upgrade`/`sec-websocket-key` kept | `src/adapters/remote.rs:444-514` (`read_request`). No `cookie`, `origin`, `host`, `user-agent` field exists on `RemoteRequest` (`:360-372`). |
30	| Response writer: **always** `Content-Type: application/json`, fixed headers, no way to add headers or another type | `respond` `src/adapters/remote.rs:530-553`; status reason table has no 304/302/405-specific others |
31	| Pools (4 unauth / 12 paired), rate windows keyed by exact path (`PAIR_PATH`, `INFO_PATH`) | `:567-640`; `Limits::limited` `:631` returns false for any other path |
32	| Connection loop; a connection joins the paired pool on its first reply with `authenticated: true` | `connection` `src/adapters/remote.rs:770-875` |
33	| Frame routing: everything outside `/api/v1/` is 404 here | `serve_remote` `src/app.rs:3017-3024`; match arms `:3044-3117` |
34	| Bearer auth | `authenticate` `src/app.rs:3127-3152` (bearer only) |
35	| Events socket: auth then `remote_subscribe`; revocation drops the queue → socket closes | `src/app.rs:3036`, `:2723-2760`, revoke at `:486-497` |
36	| `/info` (capabilities list, `spki_sha256`, `pairing_open`) | `remote_info` `src/app.rs:3568-3599` |
37	| `/pair`: checks window, `spki_sha256`, code; counts failures; mints token; reply is JSON with `token` | `remote_pair` `src/app.rs:3606-3673` |
38	| Envelope `{epoch, revision, body}`; refusals | `envelope` `:3730`, `refuse` `:3754` |
39	| Pairing window UI and the QR payload (JSON `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`) | `src/ui/remote.rs:140-215`; payload built `:160-167`; QR from `qr_texture` `:280`; "Copy invite" `:197-206`; redaction sentence `:72` |
40	| Pairing state | `src/core/remote.rs` (window, code, failures; `RevokeDevice` `:86`, `SetDeviceScope` `:96`) |
41	| Cert/identity: `make_identity` makes a cert with **empty SAN list** and CN `Switchboard <id>` | `src/adapters/remote.rs:95-126` |
42	| Native text pairing: `PairingInvite.parse` decodes JSON only | `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:90-120`; CLI `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:107-125` (one arg = invite, or `host:port code key`) |
43	| Fixtures / tests that must stay green | `tests/remote.rs` (`http` helper `:245`, `pair` `:406`, allowlist test `:682`, fixtures `:1587`, `:1828`; subscribe helper `:1960`); `client/Fixtures` |
44	| Docs to amend | `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1, §4.3, §5, §11, §13; `docs/design.md` remote status (`:3107`); `README.md` Layout (src/adapters/remote.rs row, tests/remote.rs row, new `web/` row); `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased |
45	| No `web/` directory exists yet | |
46	
47	## 3. Findings that change the plan
48	
49	1. **The certificate has no subject alternative name.** `CertificateParams::new(Vec::new())` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:99`). Native clients pin the SPKI and ignore names. Browsers validate the name against the host in the URL (an IP such as `192.168.x.y`, or `localhost`). With no SAN every browser reports a *name mismatch* as well as "self-signed", and iOS Safari's click-through for it is flakier. This needs fixing for the feature (and it is additive, because the SPKI is unchanged): add IP and DNS SANs, which means the cert must be **reissued from the same key** on address change. The spec already says (§5) a reissue from the same key keeps pins valid, but `identity.json` currently stores one certificate made once. Settle: SANs for the current LAN addresses + `localhost` + `<hostname>.local`, reissued from the stored key when the address set changes (key is in the Keychain; `make_identity` generates both together today, so a "reissue cert from key" function is new). Also rcgen's default validity is very long; iOS only honours "trust this certificate" profiles for ≤398 days, so if decision 1 picks certificate download, validity and `serverAuth` EKU must be set explicitly. This is the main hidden cost of the issue.
50	2. **There is no clean way to pin in a browser. State it plainly (decision 1).** Recommendation: **the click-through is the trust step, said in the paired-devices dialog; do not offer a certificate download in this cut.**
51	   - Why: a download means a configuration profile on iOS and a Keychain import on macOS: it makes the owner install a root-trust-adjacent artifact on a phone, which is more dangerous than the problem, needs the 398-day/EKU/SAN work above, and has to be served by the same unauthenticated port.
52	   - What the click-through buys: the browser remembers the exception for that origin and the channel is encrypted to whoever answered. What it does not buy: authenticity of the first page. The `key` in the URL protects against an impostor `/info`, but an impostor serving the page can omit the check and read the code. Say this in the dialog sentence. The QR is out of band, so the real protection is that the code is 40 bits, single-use, three attempts globally (§5), and only the owner's screen shows it.
53	   - A compensating step worth the plan's attention: show the key's short form (`short_hash`, `src/ui/remote.rs:303`) **on the page** after pairing and in the paired-devices row, so the owner can compare by eye as the headset flow does.
54	3. **Token transport (decision 2): recommend the cookie.** Reasons: `fetch` and `new WebSocket` both send it without script access; `localStorage` is readable by any script on the origin; the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` route needs the token in script memory and in a header that proxies/log lines see, and the host would have to echo the subprotocol. Costs the plan must include:
55	   - `RemoteRequest` gains `cookie` (take only the `sb_token`-named cookie out of the headers, as the bearer is taken out so it is "never logged with them", `src/adapters/remote.rs:355-358`); `authenticate` reads bearer, else cookie. Additive.
56	   - `RemoteReply` needs a way to add a `Set-Cookie` header on the `/pair` reply and to set a content type/headers for static files. `respond` (`:530`) hard-codes the head; change `RemoteReply` additively (a `headers: Vec<(&'static str,String)>` or a `content_type` plus extras) with `Default`-style helpers so the ~40 constructors in `app.rs` keep compiling. Check how many sites build `RemoteReply { .. }` literally (many: `app.rs:1675`, `:1684`, `:3570` and others) before choosing. A constructor-based or `..Default` change is cheaper.
57	   - **Cookie auth opens CSRF and cross-site WebSocket hijack that bearer headers never had.** `SameSite=Strict` covers most, but a LAN page on another origin at the *same host different port* is same-site. Require on every cookie-authenticated request that mutates, and on the WebSocket upgrade: `Origin` equals `https://<Host header>`. That means parsing `origin` and `host` too. Bearer-header requests skip the check. `Secure` works on an untrusted self-signed origin once the exception is accepted. Add the `Path=/`, and `Max-Age` long (the token does not expire; revocation is the control).
58	   - Cookies are per host, not per port (browsers ignore the port for cookie scoping): two Switchboard hosts on one machine/IP with different ports would **overwrite each other's cookie**. Name the cookie with the port or the first 8 chars of the `server_id` (`sb_<id8>`), or accept one-host-per-address and say so. Recommend the id-suffixed name; it also makes "identity changed" detectable.
59	   - The pairing reply must keep returning the token in the JSON body for native clients (do not change the body), and *also* set the cookie, only when the request carries a marker (e.g. an `X-Switchboard-Web: 1` header or `"web": true` in the body) so the CLI does not receive cookies.
60	4. **The "one-line excerpt the card shows" is not on the wire.** `last_message` lives on the record from the Stop hook (`src/adapters/hooks.rs:71`, `src/bin/switchboard-hook.rs:37`); `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has no such field and `docs/remote-client.md` §4.3 says the card excerpt is the record's `last_message`, "a field of the session's metadata". Either add an additive, redacted, 4 KiB-bounded `last_message` (or `excerpt`) to `SessionView`, which then flows through the fingerprint (`src/core/revision.rs`) and the Swift fixtures (decoding must stay tolerant: the Swift side decodes with defaults for new fields, check `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Views.swift`), or the page shows state + `waiting_reason` only and fetches `last-response` on open. The issue says "no new read model unless the page cannot do without one"; I'd say the card excerpt is that case, and the plan should do it through the redaction path (§4.3: card excerpt "masked from the turn's full text, then cut"). Confirm with `rg last_message src/app.rs` — it is not served today.
61	5. **Pool accounting for a browser page load (decision 4).** A browser opens up to 6 parallel connections per origin, each is an unauthenticated connection until its first reply with `authenticated: true`. The static files return `authenticated: false` forever, so a connection that only serves page files stays in the pool of 4 and a 5th simultaneous connection is closed at accept. With HTTP/1.1 keep-alive the page, CSS and JS share connections, but Chrome speculatively opens extra ones. Plan: (a) serve the page from a small number of files (`/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css`, maybe one favicon response) and put CSS+JS inline-free but few; (b) the page's own `fetch` carrying the cookie will make a connection move to the paired pool on its first authenticated reply, which already works; (c) the static route needs its own rate window (it is not covered by `Limits::limited`, `:631`): e.g. 120/minute per listener, counted in the connection thread, answered 429 before the frame. Static bytes should be answered **on the connection thread, not the frame**: they are `&'static str`, need no core state, and would otherwise occupy the 64-slot inbox and the 8-per-pass drain. The one wrinkle is that `serve_remote` is where the allowlist lives today; the new allowlist for static paths would live in the adapter (`connection`), which §4.1 says must be "thin"; keep it to an exact-match table, fixed at compile time. This also keeps §5's "nothing before pairing but `/info`, `/pair` and now the page itself" true by construction: the static table is closed and contains no host data.
62	6. **Allowlist change in the spec.** "Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" (`src/app.rs:3023`, spec §4.3 "refused before translation") becomes: exact `GET` of `/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css` (and optional `/favicon.ico` → 204/404) served; every other non-`/api/v1/` path remains 404. Methods other than GET/HEAD on those → 405 (`405` already in the reason table). `GET /` with the pairing query is the same document.
63	7. **Headers for the static answers (decision 4).** Proposed set, all tested in `tests/remote.rs`:
64	   - `/`: `text/html; charset=utf-8`; `/app.js`: `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`; `/app.css`: `text/css; charset=utf-8`.
65	   - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'` covers `wss:` same-origin in current browsers; Safari older than 15.4 did not match `'self'` for WebSocket, so add `wss:` explicitly if testing shows it (cannot be tested without a browser: note as a known risk).
66	   - `Cache-Control: no-store` (the page carries no secrets, but "no caching across versions" in the issue; an `ETag` of the build version is the alternative and also fine, but `no-store` is simplest and the files are small). `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (the URL briefly carries the code), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.
67	   - The pairing URL query reaches the server in the request line; it is parsed into `RemoteRequest.query` and the code must **not** be logged: `refuse`/log lines print `request.path` only (no query) already (`src/app.rs:3760`), keep it so. The page script strips it with `history.replaceState` first. `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` stops it leaking via referrer; the history entry is replaced before any navigation.
68	   - Also make the code in the URL harmless after the fact: it is single-use and closes the window on success, which is already true.
69	8. **Version skew between page and host:** page is `include_str!`ed so it always matches the binary; the page should read `protocol` from `/info` (`REMOTE_PROTOCOL`) and refuse a higher major, as the Swift client does.
70	9. **URL form for the QR (decision 3): one URL, keep the JSON as parse-only compatibility.** `https://<address>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`. Everything is URL-safe (Crockford code, hex key, UUID). Changes: `src/ui/remote.rs:160` builds the URL (needs a non-empty address; when `local_address()` is `None` fall back to the JSON/no QR, since the URL needs a host); "Copy invite" copies the URL; the multiple `addresses` in the JSON collapse to one, so choose the address a phone can reach (`remote::local_address()`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:962`). `PairingInvite.parse` (Swift) and the CLI must accept both: if the text starts with `https://`, parse host:port and the three query items, else JSON. Keep JSON decoding for old hosts ↔ new clients (a new client against an old host's pasted JSON; an old CLI cannot read the new URL, which is the one forward-compat break to say in the changelog). Add a Swift fixture and a parse test, and a Rust test that the UI payload parses. The headset's typed-code path and Bonjour path need no change. There is no reason to keep two QRs.
71	10. **Revocation visibility.** Revoke drops the subscriber queue so the socket closes (`src/app.rs:486`); the page then re-requests, gets 401 `unauthorized`, and shows "revoked". The page cannot tell "revoked" from "token never valid" except by having been paired earlier in this origin (cookie present at load, 401 on first call). Say "This device was revoked or the host forgot it. Pair again." Key rotation → new `spki_sha256` from `/info` ≠ remembered → "identity changed, pair again", and the page sends nothing.
72	11. **`/info` rate limit** (60/min per listener, `INFO_PER_MINUTE` `:584`) is shared by every browser load and by the page's reconnect loop. The page must call `/info` once per load, not per poll, and back off on 429.
73	12. **Reply by revision and the events socket from a browser.** Page needs: `hello` first; buffer events; snapshot; reconcile (§4.4). Browser `WebSocket` cannot set headers, so with the cookie it just connects to `wss://<host>/api/v1/events`. The frame sends `watch`/`unwatch` text frames the same as native. Subscriber `all` (scope=all) is not wanted: workers hidden.
74	13. **Waiting-first grouping needs only existing data:** `GET waiting` and `SessionView.waiting`, `card`, `kind`, `waiting_reason`. "A session that starts waiting moves to the top without a reload" = a `changed {waiting}` / `changed {session}` event, then refetch.
75	14. **Reply box:** posts `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` with an `op` (UUID via `crypto.randomUUID()`, which needs a secure context: fine under HTTPS even self-signed once excepted) and handles the three op statuses from `/ops/{op}` (§4.5): never resubmit on `interrupted`. Hidden unless the device's scope is `control`: scope is **not returned by any authenticated read today**. `/pair` returns it once; on a later load the page has only the cookie. Need a source: add an additive `scope` (and `device_name`) to an authenticated reply. Cheapest: a new `GET /api/v1/me` -> `{name, scope, server_name}` or extend `/info` with a `device` object when authenticated (`remote_info` is reached before `authenticate`, `src/app.rs:3028`, so `/info` would need to peek at the cookie/bearer). Prefer a new `GET /api/v1/device`, behind auth, read scope: one new arm in `serve_remote` plus the doc row. A scope lowered in the dialog (`SetDeviceScope`) then shows on the next call; the page should re-read it on a 403.
76	15. **Dispatch tickets / draft / dictation endpoints stay unused** (out of cut).
77	
78	## 4. Proposed shape (for the plan)
79	
80	Order, each a working app, smallest first (CLAUDE.md "Adding a feature" and one-commit milestones):
81	
82	1. **Cert SANs.** `make_identity`/reissue from the stored key; tests: SPKI unchanged across reissue; native pin still verifies; the cert lists the LAN IP and `localhost`. (`src/adapters/remote.rs`, `tests/remote.rs` `a_change_of_address_rebinds_the_port` `:1493` is the neighbor.)
83	2. **Adapter plumbing:** `RemoteRequest { cookie, origin, host }`, `RemoteReply` headers/content type, a closed static table answered in `connection` with its own rate window and pool behavior; `respond` takes headers. Unit tests in the adapter.
84	3. **Host API additions:** cookie auth in `authenticate`, `Set-Cookie` on a web `/pair`, Origin check for cookie-authenticated POST/upgrade, `GET /api/v1/device`, excerpt on `SessionView` (control crate additive) with fingerprint and fixtures. Core test where state moves (none expected: no new core state).
85	4. **`web/` (index.html, app.js, app.css)** embedded with `include_str!`; no build step. `web/` row in README Layout. Plain JS, no inline script (CSP).
86	5. **QR becomes the URL**; Swift `PairingInvite.parse` and CLI accept URL or JSON; script/dev-aid unchanged except README note on "Copy invite".
87	6. **Docs:** remote-client.md §4.1 (static pool), §4.3 (static paths table and `device`), §5 (cookie, Origin, click-through, key on page, URL form, dialog sentence), §11 tests, §13 decisions; design.md remote status; CHANGELOG Unreleased line; the paired-devices dialog sentence in `src/ui/remote.rs`.
88	
89	## 5. Tests (decision 5)
90	
91	- `tests/remote.rs`, over the real TLS listener with the existing `http` helper (`:245`; it must be extended to return headers, today it returns status + body only):
92	  - Each static path answers 200 with its Content-Type, CSP, `no-store`, `nosniff`; unknown non-`/api/v1/` path 404; POST to `/` 405; `HEAD` handled or refused consistently.
93	  - **Embedded-page consistency:** scan `web/index.html` and `web/app.js` for `src=`, `href=`, and `fetch(`/`WebSocket(` string literals; every one is either a served static path or begins `/api/v1/` and matches a route in the allowlist (assert against a list exported from the adapter, not a hand-copy). No `http://`/`https://` externals, no `<script>` without `src`, no inline `on*=` handlers or `style=` (CSP).
94	  - Pairing end-to-end with the host's own HTTP client as the CLI does: open window, GET `/?code=...` (200, static), GET `/api/v1/info`, check key equality, POST `/pair` with the web marker, assert `Set-Cookie` has `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`, then GET `/api/v1/waiting` using only the cookie; assert JSON body of `/pair` still has the token for the non-web path and **no** cookie there.
95	  - Cookie auth: Origin mismatch refused on POST `send` and on the upgrade; no Origin with bearer allowed; cookie from the wrong `server_id` suffix ignored; revoke → next cookie request 401; lowered scope → `send` refused 403 with the `control` scope message.
96	  - Static paths do not consume the frame inbox (flood 200 `GET /` and assert a paired metadata request is still answered in a pass) and respect the new rate window; unauthenticated pool of 4 unaffected for paired clients (existing stalled-strangers test pattern).
97	  - The pairing URL parse: a Rust unit test in `src/ui/remote.rs` that the payload is a URL whose three query items round-trip; Swift test for URL and JSON invite; a fixture in `client/Fixtures`.
98	- No test drives a browser (as the issue says). The `history.replaceState`-first ordering and the key comparison are JS that cannot be tested in CI here; state that, keep `app.js` small with these two lines first, and do one manual run per CLAUDE.md "Driving the live app" with `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR`/`SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` on test locations and screenshot a headless browser if any is available.
99	
100	## 6. Risks and open questions for the owner
101	
102	- Certificate SANs and browser acceptance on iOS Safari cannot be verified from CI. The plan should list a manual acceptance on a real phone (the issue's acceptance paragraph).
103	- Cookie `Secure` over a self-signed exception works in Safari/Chrome; Firefox is stricter about exceptions per origin with a changed SAN set. Reissuing the cert when the address changes invalidates the browser's saved exception: the owner clicks through again (not a pairing loss, since the key is the same and the cookie stays).
104	- The URL puts the code in the request line the host receives (and in the QR image). The host logs path only. Browser history: removed by `replaceState`, but the initial navigation entry is already recorded by some browsers before script runs; mitigate with the single-use code and 5-minute window, and say so.
105	- Mixed content: the page is `https`, so the QR must be `https://`. Phones that scan and offer "open in browser" may preview the URL (some scanners fetch it server-side; here it is a LAN address so they cannot).
106	- Multi-host on one IP and cookie scoping (finding 3).
107	- Is the Bonjour-name (`<hostname>.local`) wanted as a second address in the SANs? Not required for the first cut.
108	- Whether to extend `SessionView` with the excerpt (finding 4) or drop the excerpt for the first cut. Recommendation: add it (additive, redacted).
109	
110	## 7. Not touched / confirmed constraints
111	
112	- No change to `model.rs` (no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump), no new on-disk file, no new dependency for the page; maybe none for the host (cookie and header parsing by hand in the existing reader).
113	- Hard rules respected by the plan: nothing written into project dirs; no secrets in the URL beyond the single-use code; no `~/.claude/settings.json` change; no client names anywhere.
114	- Commit hygiene reminder for the implementer: no tool attribution lines in commits or PR bodies (CLAUDE.md overrides the harness reminder), check the body for `claude.ai` before `gh pr create`.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 11. Tests and failure cases

Host, in `tests/remote.rs` and the adapter's own tests unless said otherwise:

- Two hosts produce the same `RecordId` (seeded in fakes): no collision in UI or routing (client).
- A host's IP changes; Bonjour rediscovers it under the same pinned key (client, spike).
- Two advertisements claim one `server_id` with different keys: no automatic trust or merge (client).
- A substituted certificate during first pairing: the client refuses to send the code; and a `/pair` carrying another host's `spki_sha256` is refused by the host.
- Three wrong codes from three concurrent connections close the one pairing window; a fourth, correct, is refused. A consumed code is refused on the next `/pair`. Twenty unauthenticated connections and a `/pair` flood past the per-minute cap: a paired client's requests are answered throughout, the flood gets 429 and closed sockets.
- After Revoke, the device's next request fails and its WebSocket is closed. After a key rotation, `devices.json` is empty, every old token fails, and the dialog says the pairings are gone; the client, seeing the new key under a known `server_id`, sends nothing and asks to pair again.
- A scope lowered in the dialog refuses the device's next `send`; raised, allows it; no request over the port changes a scope.
- A mutation dispatched between a subscriber's `hello` and its first snapshot, and another during a multi-resource sync: the client ends with the host's state (host test on the ordering, client test on the reconciliation).
- An older snapshot reply arriving after a newer one is dropped by revision (client).
- The host restarts: the new `epoch` makes the client refetch everything.
- A `send` whose process is killed after the keys went into the pane and before the reply line (the fake host records the write, the fake log fails the reply append): the retry with the same op is answered `interrupted` and nothing is sent twice. A failed request-line append refuses the send and sends nothing. A dropped HTTP response after a logged reply is answered from the log.
- `unknown` for an op that never reached the frame; a resubmit runs once.
- The configured secret appears in a prompt, a tool result, a final response, a run's output, and a pinned non-dotenv text file: every content endpoint returns it masked. A secret store that fails makes every content endpoint refuse rather than answer.
- The configured secret straddles each cut: the parser's `DETAIL_CAP` inside a tool result, the 256 KiB turn cut, the first byte of a run-output tail window, and the front cut of a last response: each reply masks it whole or drops it whole, never a fragment.
- A project with three hundred sessions, each with 64 KiB notes and a 100 KiB `name`, listed whole: one reply under the cap, notes cut at 4 KiB and names at 4 KiB with each field in `truncated`, no member lost; the same session read alone carries its notes whole. A session entering and leaving `waiting` emits `changed {waiting}` and the refetched collection lacks or holds it accordingly; a member missing from a whole reply at a later revision is dropped by the client, a member missing from an older reply arriving late is not.
- A 700 KiB file of quotation marks is under the source limit and answers `too_large` from the serialized check; a pane with 200 lines of 4 KiB each is cut by bytes after masking and marked. A pinned file over the source limit answers `too_large`; a last response over the body cap is cut from the front and marked.
- Content versions (F2): a pinned file rewritten in place at the same size with its mtime restored, a file replaced by rename, a run log truncated and regrown to its old length, and a transcript appended twice within one poll interval: each read after the change carries new content and a new revision, and no two different bodies for one key share a revision within an epoch. Two reads of an unchanged file carry the same revision.
- Frame cost (F4): a 20 MiB transcript, a 768 KiB file and a Keychain read made to block for two seconds, each requested while a second connection reads session metadata: the metadata reply arrives within a pass and the frame's time per pass stays under its budget; only the requesting connection waits. A content handle read on the frame for a record removed before the worker finishes: the worker's version action is a no-op and the reply names the handle it read.
- A window on the last response alone, and one on the conversation, each refresh when the transcript grows with no session metadata change; a handle rebind refreshes both.
- With every content cache populated, a new environment-set grant, a changed secret value, and a secret store that starts failing: unchanged screen, file and run-output sources are not served from their old masked bytes; the first two emit `changed` for the watched keys and serve newly masked text, the third refuses.
- A watched session's transcript grows and a watched pinned file is edited while the host shows an unrelated project, a document, the Dispatch page, and while the window is hidden: `changed` arrives within the poll interval.
- A space rename, a session moved between projects, a project and a session removed, a time-based rule set losing a member: the right `changed` and `removed` events, no reconnect.
- A set renamed and a pin moved (saved through `SaveViews`), a Claude Code pane reaching its trust question (`PromptSeen`, no save), and a Codex pane passing its quiet interval (`HostListed`, no save, no screen change): each emits `changed` for the right resource within the pass. Ten passes over a running pane with nothing else moving emit nothing, though `quiet_secs` moved on each.
- Two reads of a watched file, a transcript and a pane separated by an external edit with no poll between them, delivered to the client in reverse order: the client ends on the newer content. A read of a session's metadata between them does not invalidate the conversation page.
- Closing one of two windows on a session sends no `unwatch`; closing the second does. A hundred and twenty-nine watched keys against the cap of 128: the least recently read is evicted, a read of it still answers with the right version and re-enters it, and no watch is refused. Reconnect resends the watches before any snapshot.
- Forget server on the client removes its token, pin, memory and views; a revocation seen on a connection drops the token and memory and keeps the views marked; nothing from a host is found on the client's disk after a relaunch (client).
- The subscriber queue overflows: `resync_required`, the socket closes, the host's frame loop and a second subscriber are unaffected (spike and adapter test).
- 20 stalled unauthenticated connections: the port stays answerable to a paired client (spike).
- `read_pinned`: a pin with `..`, an absolute path, an empty component; a symlink as a parent component (inside or outside the root, both refused) and as the leaf; a parent directory swapped for a symlink between two hops of the walk, driven from a second thread; a file that grows past the limit during the read; a FIFO with no writer, asserting the refusal returns at once and an unrelated request completes meanwhile; a directory and a device as the leaf. Each refused or capped as §4.3 says.
- A long transcript pages by turn; one enormous turn is cut and marked; a conversation whose handle changed answers with the new `resume_id` and the client refetches from 1 (client).
- An exited command whose pane is gone: `screen` refuses, `runs` and `run_output` answer from the log; a pruned log answers with the reason.
- Several windows show one session with independent view state and consistent data (client).
- A request outside the allowlist (`env.resolve`, `project.add`, a path that no set pins, a pinned `.env`) is refused with no side effect, and the refusal is logged by name only.
- Revocation while connected: the WebSocket closes, the next request fails with the reason, cached content stays readable on the client but is marked.
- A restart and a rebuild under the stable signing identity keep the key readable; two data directories under one macOS account keep separate keys; a missing key makes a fresh identity and the dialog says the pairings are gone.
- A `cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))` build compiles with the Bonjour adapter stubbed.

## 12. Answers to the first draft's questions

1. **Models and ids.** `src/core/model.rs`: `SessionRecord` (`RecordId`), `Project` (`ProjectId`), `WorkingSet` (`SetId`) with `PinnedItem { target: PinTarget, rect: GridRect }`, `CardState`, `Run` (a command's or service's run with its scrollback log name). Conversations are `ports::transcript::Conversation` with `Turn { n, user, activity, final_text, .. }`, read by `adapters/transcript.rs` from Claude Code's JSONL.
2. **Control port reuse.** Yes, directly: `app.rs::serve` takes a `wire::Request` and returns a `wire::Reply`; `core/control.rs` maps bodies to `ControlAction`. The remote adapter is another producer of requests for the same path, with auth, the allowlist and redaction in front, and the log-before-run step added to `serve` for non-replayable commands.
3. **Runtime.** None to own; the frame thread is the executor and `listen`/`serve_pending` are the startup and polling hooks. Shutdown drops the listener as the control socket does.
4. **Events.** No bus, and no effect that reliably marks a visible change: `Save`, `SaveViews` and `SaveSettings` are three effects, and `PromptSeen` and the quiet interval in `reconcile.rs` change a card with none of them. So the port diffs the exported read models after every pass, with the clock-derived `quiet_secs` held out of the hash, and versions content where it is read (§4.4). Retained replay is not needed: a subscriber is registered on the frame thread, so subscribe-then-snapshot has no gap.
5. **Pinned file access.** The document preview (`ui::document::Preview::load`) is a UI loader: a metadata check and then an unbounded read, which is fine for the user's own click and not for a remote reader. The port gets `read_pinned` in the files adapter: a descriptor-anchored `openat` walk with no symlink followed and a nonblocking open, as §4.3 says, run on the connection thread.
6. **Per-session UI state and polling.** `UiState` (drafts, scroll, folds) is transient and never read by the core; none of it crosses to the client. The conversation cache in `UiState` and the caption poll in `refresh_captions` both follow the local view: a session not on the Mac's screen is not polled, and a document, workflow, Dispatch or ticket view polls nothing. The app also parses a transcript synchronously on the frame (`refresh_conversation`), which one frame absorbs for one session on screen and would not for every watched session. The port therefore needs its own watch set, the cache lifted to the app, and content work on the connection and worker threads, which are the app-level changes the implementation constraint allows.
7. **Two installations.** `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` and `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` on a `switchboard-test-*` socket; only the lock holder listens; `tests/control.rs` and `tests/gate.rs` show the pattern.

**Implementation constraint:** no change to the egui frontend beyond A0's cache move, and no change to how the transcript parser reads or shapes a conversation. The host work is one adapter, additive wire views, a `read_pinned` method on the files port, an additive `read_masked` on the transcript reader (the mask runs inside the existing parse, before its detail cap) and an overlap read in `scrollback`, the content caches, read-model diff, two-step content handoff and watch worker in `app.rs`, the log-before-run step in `serve`, a Settings field or two, and one dialog. Anything larger is proposed separately.

## 13. Explicit design decisions

| Decision | v1 choice |
|---|---|
| Topology | Independent hosts, no coordinator |
| Multi-host | Concurrent connections and unified browsing |
| Resources | Sessions, projects, working sets with pins, pinned files, runs; no card resource |
| Identity | `identity.json` UUID and certificate; key in the Keychain per installation; clients pin the public key |
| Discovery | Bonjour and manual endpoints |
| Host runtime | Frame-thread dispatch for core state; content work on connection and worker threads; blocking std server with bounded queues; no Tokio |
| Contract | The `switchboard-control` wire views, extended additively, behind an allowlist |
| Data fetch | HTTPS JSON, every reply stamped with epoch and revision |
| Live changes | One WSS per host; read-model diff after every pass, content versions assigned on read, watch worker; `changed`/`removed` events; refetch |
| Synchronization | Subscribe, then snapshot, then reconcile by revision; full refetch on a new epoch |
| Idempotency | The control port's operation id and `operations.log`, non-replayable commands logged before they run |
| Redaction | One policy over every text leaving the port, run on whole source text before any cut; fail closed |
| Caps | Collections answered whole with every string bounded; only the conversation pages; scalar content cut after masking or refused whole; the limit enforced on serialized bytes |
| Content versions | Transcript: size and mtime (append-only); file and run log: inode, ctime and size; screen: hash; no two bodies share a revision for one key |
| Masked caches | Versioned by source and by the project's redaction policy fingerprint; a resolution failure refuses, never serves a cached success |
| Watch set | Global cap of 128, least recently read evicted, never refused; a read always versions correctly |
| File reads | Descriptor-anchored `openat` walk, no symlink followed, nonblocking open, 768 KiB, on the connection thread |
| Authentication | Pairing window with QR, key verified before the code is sent, 40-bit single-use code with one global attempt counter, 256-bit bearer token without expiry, scope set in the host dialog; Keychain on both ends; key rotation clears every pairing |
| Client storage | Server list and presentation state on disk, token and pin in the Keychain, every host body in memory only |
| Milestone A | Five commits: cache move, authenticated read-only host, two-host client, synchronization, watched content |
| Session execution | Always on the owning host |
| Resume | User-initiated only, confirmed on the client |
| Presentation state | Client-owned |
| visionOS layout | Native movable windows |
| Remote internet access | Deferred; protocol-compatible |
| iPadOS | Shared Swift core and views |
  seed the new place.
- **Spike 22** (`spikes/22-remote-port`). A pinned-TLS HTTP and
  WebSocket port on std threads with the frame as the executor works
  as specified: the frame's share is under 0.25 ms per pass, a
  request's latency is one frame interval (a client that sends on the
  reply synchronizes with the frame), the connection pools, the
  handshake timeout and the subscriber overflow hold under a stall and
  an unread socket, a wrong pin fails at the handshake, and `mdns-sd`
  advertises a service `dns-sd` sees. The largest transcript on this
  machine (146 MB) reads and parses in 290 ms at 575 MB peak, which
  settles that content work runs off the frame and argues for one
  content worker rather than one per connection. ctime and inode see
  the same-size rewrite, the rename and the regrown log that mtime,
  size and length miss. Not measured: the visionOS pinning delegate
  and the read-model diff.
- **A1, identity and an authenticated read-only host.** `identity.json`
  holds the server id, the display name, the self-signed certificate
  (made with `rcgen` on first start) and its SPKI hash, and where the
  port binds (loopback until the owner allows the local network, port
  43187 or `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT`); the private key is a Keychain
  item under `remote-key:<server id>`. A certificate whose key is gone
  is remade over a new key under the same id, `devices.json` is cleared
  and the dialog says so; a Keychain error keeps the identity and the
  port does not listen. `adapters/remote.rs` is the TLS listener in the
  control socket's shape, with the pools, deadlines, body cap and rate
  limits of the spec's §4.1, handing at most eight requests per pass
  to the frame; `app.rs` authenticates the bearer, routes the
  allowlist (`/info`, `/pair`, projects, spaces, sets, one set,
  sessions, one session, waiting, screen) onto the control port's
  `answer`, bounds every string in a reply (4 KiB, notes 64 KiB alone,
  each cut named in `truncated`), caps the body at 1 MiB and wraps it
  in `{epoch, revision, body}`; everything else is refused by name,
  before translation. Pairing: the Remote devices dialog (settings
  menu) opens a five-minute window with an eight-character Crockford
  code shown as a QR carrying the server id, key hash, code and
  address; `/pair` must carry the host's own key hash and the code,
  three failures from any connection close the window, the first
  success spends it, and the device gets a 43-character bearer token
  whose SHA-256 is what `devices.json` keeps. The dialog lists devices
  with scope (read or control, changed there and nowhere else), last
  seen and Revoke. Not in A1: events, the content worker (the screen
  is answered on the frame as the control port answers it, until the
  screen cache of A4), Bonjour (A2), and `server_name` lives in
  `identity.json` rather than `Settings`, which the spec now says.
- **A2, two hosts and the first client.** The host advertises
  `_switchboard._tcp` through `mdns-sd` (`adapters/bonjour.rs`, a stub

## 11. Tests and failure cases

Host, in `tests/remote.rs` and the adapter's own tests unless said otherwise:

Twenty unauthenticated connections and a `/pair` flood past the per-minute cap: a paired client's requests are answered throughout, the flood gets 429 and closed sockets.

## 12. Answers to the first draft's questions

1. **Models and ids.** `src/core/model.rs`: `SessionRecord` (`RecordId`), `Project` (`ProjectId`), `WorkingSet` (`SetId`) with `PinnedItem { target: PinTarget, rect: GridRect }`, `CardState`, `Run` (a command's or service's run with its scrollback log name). Conversations are `ports::transcript::Conversation` with `Turn { n, user, activity, final_text, .. }`, read by `adapters/transcript.rs` from Claude Code's JSONL.
2. **Control port reuse.** Yes, directly: `app.rs::serve` takes a `wire::Request` and returns a `wire::Reply`; `core/control.rs` maps bodies to `ControlAction`. The remote adapter is another producer of requests for the same path, with auth, the allowlist and redaction in front, and the log-before-run step added to `serve` for non-replayable commands.
3. **Runtime.** None to own; the frame thread is the executor and `listen`/`serve_pending` are the startup and polling hooks. Shutdown drops the listener as the control socket does.
4. **Events.** No bus, and no effect that reliably marks a visible change: `Save`, `SaveViews` and `SaveSettings` are three effects, and `PromptSeen` and the quiet interval in `reconcile.rs` change a card with none of them. So the port diffs the exported read models after every pass, with the clock-derived `quiet_secs` held out of the hash, and versions content where it is read (§4.4). Retained replay is not needed: a subscriber is registered on the frame thread, so subscribe-then-snapshot has no gap.
5. **Pinned file access.** The document preview (`ui::document::Preview::load`) is a UI loader: a metadata check and then an unbounded read, which is fine for the user's own click and not for a remote reader. The port gets `read_pinned` in the files adapter: a descriptor-anchored `openat` walk with no symlink followed and a nonblocking open, as §4.3 says, run on the connection thread.
6. **Per-session UI state and polling.** `UiState` (drafts, scroll, folds) is transient and never read by the core; none of it crosses to the client. The conversation cache in `UiState` and the caption poll in `refresh_captions` both follow the local view: a session not on the Mac's screen is not polled, and a document, workflow, Dispatch or ticket view polls nothing. The app also parses a transcript synchronously on the frame (`refresh_conversation`), which one frame absorbs for one session on screen and would not for every watched session. The port therefore needs its own watch set, the cache lifted to the app, and content work on the connection and worker threads, which are the app-level changes the implementation constraint allows.
7. **Two installations.** `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` and `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET` on a `switchboard-test-*` socket; only the lock holder listens; `tests/control.rs` and `tests/gate.rs` show the pattern.

**Implementation constraint:** no change to the egui frontend beyond A0's cache move, and no change to how the transcript parser reads or shapes a conversation. The host work is one adapter, additive wire views, a `read_pinned` method on the files port, an additive `read_masked` on the transcript reader (the mask runs inside the existing parse, before its detail cap) and an overlap read in `scrollback`, the content caches, read-model diff, two-step content handoff and watch worker in `app.rs`, the log-before-run step in `serve`, a Settings field or two, and one dialog. Anything larger is proposed separately.

## 4. Rust host

### 4.1 Implementation

- **No Tokio.** The host is std threads and `mpsc`; the core is owned by `SwitchboardApp` and every state change is a dispatch on the frame thread. The remote port follows the `ControlSocket` shape: an accept thread per listener, one thread per connection, each request handed over a channel to the frame, answered by the same `serve` path in `app.rs` (`serve_pending` runs before every frame, hidden ones included), the reply sent back on the connection's channel. A second runtime inside an egui app buys nothing for a handful of connections.
- **The frame does core state only.** A metadata request (a view, a command) is answered on the frame as the control port is. A content request (conversation, screen, run output, file) takes two steps: the frame answers with the **handle and the redaction policy** (the transcript path and resume handle, the pane's host id, the run's log path, the file's root and relative path, plus the secret values to mask and the policy fingerprint), and one **content worker thread** does the read, the parse, the mask, the version check and the serialization from a queue of such requests (one at a time, so one large parse is in memory at once; Spike 22 measured 575 MB peak for the largest transcript), then sends one small action back to the frame to record the version it observed (§4.4), and the connection thread writes the reply. The watch poll (§4.4) runs through the same worker. A multi-megabyte transcript, a 768 KiB file or a slow Keychain call therefore costs the worker its time and the asking connection its wait, never a frame. The handle is read under the frame's authority, so a record removed or rebound between the two steps makes the worker's version action a no-op and the reply carries the handle it read from.
- **Bounds.** The port is one user's few devices, and the limits say so:
  - at most 16 connections in total and 4 unauthenticated ones; a further accept is closed at once. The 4 are a separate pool: an unauthenticated flood fills its own slots and never a paired client's;
  - `/pair` is answered at most six times a minute per listener and `/info` sixty; past that the connection thread answers 429 without reaching the frame;
  - a TLS handshake and the first request line each within 5 s, a request body within 10 s, a write within 10 s; a connection that misses a deadline is closed;
  - one request in flight per connection (HTTP/1.1, no pipelining);
  - the frame drains at most 8 remote requests per pass, in arrival order, the rest waiting on the channel; the channel is bounded at 64 and a full channel answers 503 from the connection thread without reaching the frame; a frame-side request is a view or a handle lookup and takes microseconds, so the count is the bound;
  - each WebSocket subscriber has an event queue of 256; when it fills, the subscriber is sent `resync_required` and closed, never silently trimmed (§4.4);
  - the watch set (§4.4) is capped at 128 keys for the whole port; past the cap the least recently read key is evicted silently, since a read of an evicted key always works and re-enters it.
- Preferred crates: a blocking HTTP/1.1 server over `std::net::TcpListener` (hand-rolled or `tiny_http`), `tungstenite` for WebSocket, `rustls` with `rcgen` for the per-installation certificate, and `mdns-sd` (or the system `dns-sd` through a small macOS adapter) for Bonjour. All of it in `src/adapters/remote.rs` behind a `ports::remote` trait with a fake, and all of it must compile on Linux CI (Bonjour may be a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` adapter with a no-op elsewhere). **Spike 22 (§10) decides the exact crates before any of this is built.**
- Handlers are thin: HTTP request → auth and scope check → allowlist → `wire::Request` → `serve` → redaction → `wire::Reply` → HTTP response. No session or transcript logic lives in the adapter.
- Only the instance holding the store lock listens (as the control port does); a read-only instance refuses to bind.
- Bind to loopback by default until remote access is explicitly enabled in Settings. For LAN access, bind the chosen interface and require pairing.

What this covers is exactly the values Switchboard holds: a secret the user pasted into a prompt, or one a tool printed that Switchboard never knew, is not found. The paired-devices dialog says this in a sentence, and the claim in design.md's trust boundary is widened to "or as redacted text on the remote port".

New read models, added to the wire crate:

- `session.conversation`: the `Conversation` from `ports::transcript` as a wire shape: title, model, branch, usage, and turns paged by **turn number** (`n`, 1-based). The host parses the whole JSONL, as the session view does, from the app-level cache (§4.4); a transcript the app can show is one the port can serve, and the supported size is whatever the app handles, which the spike measures. What paging bounds is the **response**: a page anchored at its start (`from=turn`) stops at `limit` turns or at the body cap, whichever first, and says `next` for the turn to continue from; a page anchored at its end (`from=last`, or `before=turn` for the page ending before a turn the client holds) fills backward from the anchor, so it always reaches it and `from` is wherever it filled up. The client opens on the tail and walks back with `before`, so a transcript whose turns are large never shows a stale end or a gap; a change is followed from the last turn held page after page until `next` is empty, up to ten pages. A page carries only the first 512 bytes of each tool call's input and result and of each activity's text, marked `more`, which is what keeps a turn with a hundred tool calls to tens of kilobytes rather than hundreds; `session.turn` reads one turn whole, at the conversation's revision, and the client asks for it when a turn's activity is opened. A single turn larger than 256 KiB is cut (final text kept whole where possible, activity text trimmed) and marked `truncated`. The page carries the `resume_id` it was read from: `/clear` and a discard rebind the record to a new transcript, and a client holding turn numbers from another handle drops them and refetches from 1. The last turn is always in progress until a `Stop` event: on a `changed {conversation}` the client refetches from the last turn it holds and **replaces** that turn and everything after it. A handle rebind (`resume_id` moved on the session view) changes the conversation cache's key, which emits `changed {conversation}` of its own, so the client needs no rule linking the two. Only Claude Code sessions have a conversation; Codex, shell, command and service sessions answer with a "no conversation" reason and the client falls back to `screen` (and, for commands and services, `run_output`).
- `session.last_response`: the last turn's `final_text`, its `n` and `end`. It is a **projection of the `conversation` key**: it is read from the same cache, carries the conversation's content revision, is watched by watching `conversation`, and refreshes on `changed {conversation}`; a window showing only the last response registers that watch. The compact card's one-line excerpt is not part of it: that is `last_message` from the `Stop` hook on the record, a field of the session's metadata, and moves with `changed {session}`.
- `session.runs`: a command's or service's runs as the record holds them (`Run`: `n`, started, ended, exit, artifacts' names, not their paths). `session.run_output`: the tail of one run's scrollback log (`scrollback::tail_text`, escapes stripped, `lines` clamped to 500), redacted; a run whose log was pruned or rotated answers with that reason. This is how an exited command whose pane is gone is still readable: `session.screen` refuses a session that is not running, by design.
- `file.read`: content of a file **only if some working set pins it** (`PinTarget::File` with that project and path). The read goes through a new `ports::files` method, `read_pinned(root, relative)`, not through the UI's preview loader. Confinement is by descriptors, not by path strings, so it stays valid while names change under it:
  - the relative path is rejected if it is absolute, empty, or has a `..` or `.` component, before anything touches the disk (a persisted pin can hold anything);
  - the project root is opened once as a directory descriptor (`O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`) and the walk proceeds **one component at a time** with `openat` from the previous descriptor: every directory component with `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC`, the last with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC`. A component that is a symlink fails the open (`ELOOP`), so **no symlink anywhere in the path is followed, parent or leaf**; a swap of any directory for a link between two hops is refused at the next hop, and a swap after the hop cannot move the descriptor already held. `openat` comes through a safe wrapper crate (`rustix`; or `cap-std`, which does this walk itself, if the spike prefers it); the crate-wide `unsafe` ban stands;
  - `O_NONBLOCK` on the open is what keeps a FIFO from parking the connection thread for good: the open returns at once, `fstat` on the descriptor must say regular file, and anything else (a FIFO, a socket, a device, a directory as the leaf) is refused before any read. The flag is cleared on the regular file before reading. The read runs on the content worker (§4.1), so even a stall here costs the worker its time, never a frame;
  - the read is `take(limit + 1)` with the port's limit of 768 KiB (§4.2), so growth after the check cannot exceed the limit;
  - dotenv names (`.env`, `.env.*`) are refused whatever is pinned, since those hold the project's secrets;
  - the reply carries the file's `modified` and `size` from the same descriptor, and the content is masked like every other text.
  Both platforms the crate builds on are Unix, so one implementation serves macOS and Linux CI.
- `info`: `server_id`, `server_name`, protocol version, capabilities, `epoch`, `revision`, the certificate's public-key hash (SPKI, SHA-256), the port's limits (file limit, conversation page size, body cap), and whether the pairing window is open.

Avoid a general-purpose filesystem endpoint. Paths are never accepted from the client except as the identity of an existing pin.

## 5. Security and pairing

A local network is not a trust boundary: these APIs can instruct coding agents and expose private transcripts. The repo's rules apply unchanged: secret values never reach a record, a log line, a command line, or any reply but `env.resolve` (which is not on this port) and, as redacted text, the read models of §4.3; the Keychain holds key material.

- Require pairing **before** anything but `/info` and `/pair`.
- **Host identity**: a self-signed certificate made once with `rcgen` on first listen. The certificate is in `identity.json` (§3.1); its private key is a Keychain item through the existing adapter (`adapters/keychain.rs`, service `com.sadburger.switchboard`) under the account `remote-key:<server_id>`, so two data directories under one macOS account never overwrite each other's keys. The bundle must be signed with the stable identity (`scripts/bundle.sh`) or the Keychain ACL is lost on every rebuild.
- **What the client pins** is the SPKI SHA-256 of the host's public key, not the certificate's bytes, so a certificate reissued from the same key (a new expiry) still verifies. Rotating the key is making a new identity: every pairing is invalid and the dialog says so.
- **Pairing verifies the key before the code is sent.** The code alone would let an intermediary terminate the first connection, forward the code to the real host, and take the token. So the pairing window shows a **QR code** carrying `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`, and under it the same in text: a short form of the key hash and the code. The client scans or types both; it connects, compares the hash of the key it is actually talking to with the one it was given, and only when they match sends `/pair {code, device_name, spki_sha256}`. A client without a camera (visionOS gives an app none) pairs from the host's Bonjour record instead: it resolves the record, reads `/info` under no trust, shows the key the host presented in the dialog's short form for the owner to compare by eye, and pins that key for the pairing, so the typed code reaches only the host whose key the owner checked; a substituted certificate shows its own key on the device, where the owner sees it differ. The host refuses a pairing whose `spki_sha256` is not its own, so a relayed request through a substituted certificate fails even if the code reached it. Before pairing, `/info` is served to any client and nothing in it is trusted; after pairing, every connection verifies the pin before the token is presented.
- The pairing window is opened from the settings menu as "Allow pairing for 5 minutes", the same shape as the environment setup window (`ENV_SETUP_WINDOW`, never saved). The dialog that opens it chooses the scope the pairing grants, `read` by default.
- **The code**: eight characters from the 32-character Crockford alphabet (no `I`, `L`, `O`, `U`), 40 bits, drawn from the OS random source (`getrandom`), made when the window opens and shown as the QR's `code` and in text. It is single-use: the first successful `/pair` consumes it and closes the window. **Failures count globally**: one counter in the app's state, bumped on the frame for every failed `/pair` from any connection, and the window closes at three. Concurrent attempts cannot each get three, because the frame answers them in arrival order against the one counter.
- **The token**: 32 bytes from the OS random source, base64url, 43 characters. It does not expire; the owner revokes. It is sent only as a bearer header over the pinned connection, never in a URL.
- `/pair` answers with the token and the granted scope. The host stores the device name, scope, created time, last-seen time and the token's SHA-256 in `<data dir>/devices.json` (atomic write, owner-readable); never the token. The client stores the token and the pinned key hash in its Keychain.
- **Scope changes** happen in the host's dialog: a device's scope can be raised to `control` or lowered to `read` there, taking effect on the device's next request. There is no scope request over the port.
- **Key rotation** (a missing key at listen, §3.1) **deletes every record in `devices.json`** when the new identity is made, so an old token stops working on the first request, and the dialog says the pairings are gone. A client seeing a new key for a known `server_id` shows "identity changed, pair again" and sends nothing, token included.
- Every later request carries the bearer token; the host answers with the device's scope. A Settings dialog (built the way the Environment dialog is) lists paired devices with scope, last seen, and Revoke, and states what redaction does and does not cover. Revocation removes the record, takes effect on the next request and closes the device's WebSocket.
- The client verifies the pin on every connection and on endpoint changes; a mismatch is shown as "identity changed, pair again" and never auto-merged.
- Validate input, cap request bodies at 64 KiB, cap `lines` on `screen` (the wire clamps to 200) and `run_output` (500), cap pages and bodies as §4.2 says, and keep tokens out of logs, URLs, Bonjour TXT records and crash reports. Refusals are logged by op and kind, never with content.
- Loopback-only without auth is acceptable **only inside the spike directory**. No milestone commit binds a non-loopback interface without pairing.

## 4. Rust host

### 4.1 Implementation

- **No Tokio.** The host is std threads and `mpsc`; the core is owned by `SwitchboardApp` and every state change is a dispatch on the frame thread. The remote port follows the `ControlSocket` shape: an accept thread per listener, one thread per connection, each request handed over a channel to the frame, answered by the same `serve` path in `app.rs` (`serve_pending` runs before every frame, hidden ones included), the reply sent back on the connection's channel. A second runtime inside an egui app buys nothing for a handful of connections.
- **The frame does core state only.** A metadata request (a view, a command) is answered on the frame as the control port is. A content request (conversation, screen, run output, file) takes two steps: the frame answers with the **handle and the redaction policy** (the transcript path and resume handle, the pane's host id, the run's log path, the file's root and relative path, plus the secret values to mask and the policy fingerprint), and one **content worker thread** does the read, the parse, the mask, the version check and the serialization from a queue of such requests (one at a time, so one large parse is in memory at once; Spike 22 measured 575 MB peak for the largest transcript), then sends one small action back to the frame to record the version it observed (§4.4), and the connection thread writes the reply. The watch poll (§4.4) runs through the same worker. A multi-megabyte transcript, a 768 KiB file or a slow Keychain call therefore costs the worker its time and the asking connection its wait, never a frame. The handle is read under the frame's authority, so a record removed or rebound between the two steps makes the worker's version action a no-op and the reply carries the handle it read from.
- **Bounds.** The port is one user's few devices, and the limits say so:
  - at most 16 connections in total and 4 unauthenticated ones; a further accept is closed at once. The 4 are a separate pool: an unauthenticated flood fills its own slots and never a paired client's;
  - `/pair` is answered at most six times a minute per listener and `/info` sixty; past that the connection thread answers 429 without reaching the frame;
  - a TLS handshake and the first request line each within 5 s, a request body within 10 s, a write within 10 s; a connection that misses a deadline is closed;
  - one request in flight per connection (HTTP/1.1, no pipelining);
  - the frame drains at most 8 remote requests per pass, in arrival order, the rest waiting on the channel; the channel is bounded at 64 and a full channel answers 503 from the connection thread without reaching the frame; a frame-side request is a view or a handle lookup and takes microseconds, so the count is the bound;
  - each WebSocket subscriber has an event queue of 256; when it fills, the subscriber is sent `resync_required` and closed, never silently trimmed (§4.4);
  - the watch set (§4.4) is capped at 128 keys for the whole port; past the cap the least recently read key is evicted silently, since a read of an evicted key always works and re-enters it.
- Preferred crates: a blocking HTTP/1.1 server over `std::net::TcpListener` (hand-rolled or `tiny_http`), `tungstenite` for WebSocket, `rustls` with `rcgen` for the per-installation certificate, and `mdns-sd` (or the system `dns-sd` through a small macOS adapter) for Bonjour. All of it in `src/adapters/remote.rs` behind a `ports::remote` trait with a fake, and all of it must compile on Linux CI (Bonjour may be a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` adapter with a no-op elsewhere). **Spike 22 (§10) decides the exact crates before any of this is built.**
- Handlers are thin: HTTP request → auth and scope check → allowlist → `wire::Request` → `serve` → redaction → `wire::Reply` → HTTP response. No session or transcript logic lives in the adapter.
- Only the instance holding the store lock listens (as the control port does); a read-only instance refuses to bind.
- Bind to loopback by default until remote access is explicitly enabled in Settings. For LAN access, bind the chosen interface and require pairing.
- Configurable port in `identity.json` (§3.1), default `43187`, overridable with `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT` (a dev aid, documented in the README) so two instances can run on one machine; `0` picks a free one, which the tests use.
- Advertise `_switchboard._tcp` via Bonjour only while listening on a non-loopback interface. TXT records carry the protocol major version (`v`), the display name (`name`) and the `server_id` (`id`, so a client matches a record to a known server before it connects); never a token, never key material. The instance name is the display name with a short id suffix, so two installations on one machine stay distinct.
- If Switchboard closes, the port goes away. A standalone daemon is not in scope.
